title: Comprehensive Profiling of Plasma Fatty Acid Concentrations in Young Healthy Canadian Adults
finding: GC analysis of fatty acid methyl esters from total plasma lipids of 826 fasted healthy young Canadian adults quantified 61 fatty acids: mean oleate (18:1 c9) 1285.5 ± 416.7 µmol/l, cis-vaccenate (18:1 c11) 129.2 ± 59.5 µmol/l, and trans 18:1 isomers were measurable, for example elaidate (18:1 t9) 16.5 ± 11.3 µmol/l.

title: Carnitine Inborn Errors of Metabolism
finding: Review of human carnitine metabolism and its inborn errors: the biosynthetic substrate 6-N-trimethyllysine comes from lysosomal or proteasomal breakdown of proteins carrying N-methylated lysine residues, and is converted to carnitine by TMLD, HTMLA, TMABADH and BBD (BBOX1), with OCTN2 (SLC22A5) importing carnitine into cells. Normal plasma free carnitine is given as 25 to 50 micromolar, with over 99 percent of body carnitine intracellular.

title: The polar oxy-metabolome reveals the 4-hydroxymandelate CoQ10 synthesis pathway
finding: FLAG-tagged HPDL immunopurified from human cells formed 4-hydroxymandelate from 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate, but not from tyrosine or 4-hydroxyphenyllactate, and catalytically impaired HPDL mutants formed none; 4-HMA was the most highly 18O-labelled polar metabolite in human cell lines, and HPDL knockout lowered 13C9-tyrosine labelling of CoQ10 in dense cultures, with labelling restored only by wild-type HPDL.
locator: Results: HPDL makes 4-HMA from 4-HPPA; Fig. 2c-d, Fig. 3a

title: The DNA methyltransferase-like protein DNMT3L stimulates de novo methylation by Dnmt3a
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: DNMT3L lacks the conserved catalytic domain and had no methylation activity of its own in the human 293/EBNA1 cells used. Coexpressed with murine Dnmt3a, it raised de novo methylation of replicating minichromosomes at three maternally methylated imprinting centers, at a luciferase reporter and at an integrated luciferase transgene. Coexpressed with DNMT3B it left methylation at the SNRPN imprinting center little or not changed. Limits: one cell line; the stimulation of the endogenous HOXA9 gene is reported as data not shown; the endogenous SNRPN imprinting center was not methylated; the stimulation of Dnmt3a depended on its catalytic activity.
locator: Results: first paragraph; Fig. 1, Fig. 2, Fig. 5

title: Molecular basis of renal disease. Leukotrienes and lipoxins: lipoxygenase-derived modulators of leukocyte recruitment and vascular tone in glomerulonephritis
finding: Review of lipoxygenase products in glomerulonephritis which describes lipoxin formation only by successive oxygenation of arachidonic acid at carbon 15 and carbon 5 through an unstable 5,6-epoxytetraene, by platelet 12-lipoxygenase acting on neutrophil-derived LTA4, and by neutrophil 5-lipoxygenase acting on endothelial 15(R)-HETE after aspirin treatment; no conversion of 14,15-diHETE to lipoxin B4 appears anywhere in the text or in the pathway figure.

title: Albumin modifies the metabolism of hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids via 12-lipoxygenase in human platelets
finding: In ionophore-activated human platelets in vitro, 12-lipoxygenase converted 5(S)-HETE into the 5(S),12(S)-dihydroxy product (identified by co-chromatography and UV spectra against synthetic standards) and 15(S)-HETE into the 14(R),15(S)-dihydroxy product; 600 micromolar albumin cut formation of the first by roughly 90 percent while raising formation of the second about 7-fold, and it also lifted the inhibition that 15(S)-HETE exerted on 12(S)-HETE synthesis from endogenous arachidonate. Equilibrium dialysis with Scatchard analysis gave albumin binding constants of about 1.8e5 for 15-HETE, 1.4e5 for 12-HETE and 0.9e5 for 5-HETE.
locator: Results, Albumin influence on 5-HETE metabolism (Figs. 1, 2) and Albumin influence on the metabolism of 15-HETE by platelets (Figs. 4, 5); Results, Albumin binding of hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid

title: Activity of human Δ5 and Δ6 desaturases on multiple n‐3 and n‐6 polyunsaturated fatty acids
finding: In S. cerevisiae co-expressing the human elongase ELG3 with human delta-5 or delta-6 desaturase, delta-5 desaturated 20:3n-6 and 20:4n-3, and delta-6 acted on 18:2n-6 and 18:3n-3 and on the elongation-derived C24 substrates 24:4n-6 and 24:5n-3, giving 24:5n-6 and 24:6n-3. The C24 substrates were generated inside the yeast from added 20:4n-6 and 20:5n-3, because delta-6 activity was not detected when they were added directly. No kinetics were done. The authors say their data suggest the pathway and that extension to other desaturases needs more work. The paper names the genes by GenBank accession in Methods (AF226273 for delta-5 and AF126799 for delta-6, which Leonard 2000 and Cho 1999 identify as FADS1 and FADS2). Its Introduction, summarising the cloning of three human desaturase genes by another group, says that the third gene, with no function ascribed, is unlikely to be a second human delta-5 or delta-6 desaturase; this is a statement about an unascribed function in a summary of earlier work, not a result of this paper and not proof that FADS3 has none.
locator: Results and discussion: Fig. 2 (delta-6, C18), Fig. 3 (delta-6, C24), Fig. 4 (delta-5); Introduction; Methods 2.2

title: Oxidative Inactivation of Human 5‐Lipoxygenase in Phosphatidylcholine Vesicles
finding: Recombinant human 5-lipoxygenase in phosphatidylcholine vesicles with calcium oxygenated 12-HETE at the 5-position (followed by absorbance at 270 nm). Enzyme inactivation during that reaction, and during the reaction with 5,8-icosadienoic acid, was slower (k 0.21 per min, given jointly for both substrates) than with arachidonic acid (0.65 per min in Fig. 1; 0.60 per min in the abstract and Fig. 2), about threefold. The authors read this as formation of leukotriene A4 contributing to the faster inactivation, with other mechanisms also involved. Enzyme concentration differed between figure panels. No identification of the 12-HETE oxygenation products was found in the text.
locator: Results: Dependence of the rate of 5-lipoxygenase inactivation on the structure of the substrate; Fig. 1, Fig. 2

title: Identification of the gene responsible for the cblB complementation group of vitamin B12-dependent methylmalonic aciduria
finding: MMAB was localised to chromosome 12q24 by searching bacterial genomes for genes next to the methylmalonyl-CoA mutase gene (a candidate from Archaeoglobus fulgidus probed the human database). It encodes a predicted 250-residue protein, given as 45% similar to Salmonella PduO in the abstract. In six cblB patient lines the key evidence is null-type mutations (a 5-bp frameshift deletion and two splice junction mutations). R186W is in four of the six lines and in 4 of 240 control alleles, and the authors call it uncertain as a disease mutation and a rare polymorphism. R19Q and M239K are common polymorphisms. No enzyme assay of MMAB is reported; function is inferred from mutations and similarity to PduO, and expression experiments are still needed.
locator: Abstract; Results: Identification of the MMAB cDNA; Mutations in the cblB complementation group; Table 3; Discussion

title: Identification of the gene responsible for the cblA complementation group of vitamin B12-responsive methylmalonic acidemia based on analysis of prokaryotic gene arrangements
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: MMAA was identified as the gene of the cblA complementation group. Candidate genes came from bacterial gene neighbourhoods of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (COG1703 adjacent to COG2185 in 10 of the gene neighbourhoods examined). Mutation analysis of fibroblast lines from six cblA patients found mutations in five of them: a 4-bp deletion in three lines (WG1192, WG2014, WG3080), an 8-bp insertion, a premature stop (Q94X) on one allele and a missense change (Y207C) absent from 70 control lines. The effect of the missense change was not tested, and for some lines the second allele is not identified. The 418-residue product is called a member of the AAA ATPase superfamily in the abstract, while the discussion places it in the G3E family of P-loop GTPases. The authors speculate that it is a component of a transporter or an accessory protein for cobalamin entry into mitochondria. No transport was measured.
locator: Results: Mutations in the cblA Complementation Group; Fig. 7

title: Carnitine biosynthesis by the perfused rat liver from exogenous protein-bound trimethyllysine. Metabolism of methylated lysine derivatives arising from the degradation of 6-N-[methyl-3H]lysine-labeled glycoproteins.
finding: Isolated rat livers were perfused with asialo-fetuin, asialo-orosomucoid or agalacto-orosomucoid whose lysine residues carried tritiated methyl groups: trimethylated glycoproteins were taken up and degraded, and the trimethyllysine set free was converted to 4-N-trimethylaminobutyrate, carnitine and O-acetylcarnitine, while the dimethylated glycoproteins yielded no appreciable carnitine or carnitine precursors and gave tritiated water and dimethyllysine instead. Which products accumulated depended on the receptor route, with 4-N-trimethylaminobutyrate building up in livers given the non-parenchymal substrate and acetylcarnitine dominating the medium with the parenchymal substrates.
locator: Abstract; Results: Metabolism of methylated lysine residues released in the perfused liver

title: Identification of DNMT1 (DNA methyltransferase 1) hypomorphs in somatic knockouts suggests an essential role for DNMT1 in cell survival
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: In the HCT116 lines DNMT1-/- and the double knockouts DKO1 and DKO8, the disrupted DNMT1 allele still gives a truncated protein. It lacks about 17 kDa that covers the PCNA interaction domain and part of the DMAP1 interaction domain, and it keeps the nuclear localisation signal, other N-terminal domains and the catalytic C-terminal domain. Immunoprecipitated protein was active on hemimethylated DNA in vitro. The level is about 20% of wild type in DNMT1-/- and DKO1 and about 40% in DKO8. The authors conclude that these lines carry a hypomorphic allele and are not complete knockouts. Limit: three lines were examined, not every line made.
locator: Results: DNMT1 Transcripts and Protein in HCT116 Knockout Cells; Fig. 1, Fig. 2B

title: Subcellular localization and physiological role of α-methylacyl-CoA racemase
finding: Alpha-methylacyl-CoA racemase converts several (2R)-methyl-branched acyl-CoAs to the (S) isomers that beta-oxidation can use. Subcellular fractionation showed a bimodal distribution (peroxisomes and mitochondria) in rat and human liver, mainly mitochondrial in rat and mainly peroxisomal in human; the rats had been fed 1% di(2-ethylhexyl)phthalate for 7 days. Racemase activity with 2,6-dimethylheptanoyl-CoA was absent in fibroblasts of two deficient patients, taken as evidence of a single gene. Purified recombinant enzyme converted (2R,6)-dimethylheptanoyl-CoA to the (S) form in a coupled assay with rat LCAD. The mitochondrial targeting prediction is weak and the targeting mechanism unknown.
locator: Results: Figs. 3 and 4 (fractions), Fig. 5 (in vitro), Table 1 (fibroblasts); Discussion

title: Identification of the peroxisomal β-oxidation enzymes involved in the degradation of long-chain dicarboxylic acids
finding: Beta-oxidation of 16-carbon dicarboxylic acid (C16DCA) was deficient in fibroblasts from patients lacking functional peroxisomes, so it takes place in peroxisomes. Cells from SCOX deficiency, DBP deficiency, XALD and RCDP type 1 were compared (small numbers of cell lines per defect; residual activity remained in some). Recombinant human LBP and DBP in yeast were both active on the substrates; DBP-deficient cells oxidised normally, so the authors propose LBP can take over. They suggest SCOX, LBP and DBP and SCPx, possibly with the classic 3-ketothiolase. Only C16DCA was studied as substrate. The paper uses enzyme names, not gene symbols.
locator: Results: Oxidation of [16-14C]16DCA in cultured skin fibroblasts, Table 1; recombinant LBP and DBP, Fig. 4; Discussion, Fig. 5

title: A novel case of ACOX2 deficiency leads to recognition of a third human peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: A newly identified patient with an apparent homozygous 4-bp deletion had raised plasma C27 bile acid intermediates (tauro-THCA and related) and no ACOX2 protein on immunoblot of fibroblasts. Pristanic acid beta-oxidation in fibroblasts was normal, but pristanoyl-CoA oxidase activity was reduced with considerable residual activity; a second defect is not excluded. In recombinant human ACOX expressed in yeast (C10-CoA, C16-CoA, pristanoyl-CoA, THC-CoA only), ACOX1 isoforms did not use branched-chain substrates, THC-CoA was handled only by ACOX2, pristanoyl-CoA by ACOX2 and ACOX3, and ACOX2 and ACOX3 showed some activity with C10-CoA. ACOX3 mRNA and protein were found in normal human tissues.
locator: Results 3.1 with Table 1 and Fig. 1; 3.2 with Fig. 2; 3.3 with Figs. 3 and 4

title: A novel case of ACOX2 deficiency leads to recognition of a third human peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: From yeast-expressed recombinant human ACOX1, ACOX2 and ACOX3 tested on four substrates and from tissue expression (ACOX2 almost exclusive to liver and kidney), the authors conclude that ACOX2 is the only acyl-CoA oxidase in human bile acid synthesis (THC-CoA handled only by ACOX2). ACOX1 oxidises straight-chain fatty acids of different chain lengths, and both ACOX2 and ACOX3 handle pristanoyl-CoA. ACOX2 and ACOX3 also showed some C10-CoA activity. Evidence comes from one ACOX2-deficient patient with normal pristanic acid oxidation in fibroblasts (reduced pristanoyl-CoA oxidase activity), whose ACOX3 expression was detected. The text does not state the stereoisomer of THC-CoA that was used.
locator: Discussion (paragraph on substrate specificity and tissue expression); Results 3.2 with Fig. 2; 3.3

title: A novel case of ACOX2 deficiency leads to recognition of a third human peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: Substrate specificity tests of yeast-expressed recombinant human ACOX1, ACOX2 and ACOX3 (C10-CoA, C16-CoA, pristanoyl-CoA, THC-CoA only) show that ACOX1 oxidises straight-chain acyl-CoAs of different chain lengths (the two ACOX1 isoforms differ in preference) and is not active on the branched-chain substrates; ACOX2 alone handled THC-CoA, and ACOX2 and ACOX3 both handled pristanoyl-CoA. ACOX2 and ACOX3 also showed some activity with C10-CoA, so straight-chain substrates are not strictly excluded. The work was prompted by an ACOX2-deficient patient with normal pristanic acid oxidation in fibroblasts.

title: Mechanisms in anti-inflammation and resolution: the role of lipoxins and aspirin-triggered lipoxins
journal: Brazilian Journal of Medical and Biological Research
finding: Review of lipoxins and aspirin-triggered lipoxins which sets out three transcellular routes to lipoxin A4 and lipoxin B4, namely 15-lipoxygenase products of airway epithelial cells or monocytes converted by neutrophil 5-lipoxygenase via a 5S,6S,15S-epoxytetraene, LTA4 passed from myeloid cells to platelet 12-lipoxygenase, and acetylated COX-2-derived 15R-HETE converted by leukocyte 5-lipoxygenase to the 15-epimer lipoxins; no formation of lipoxin B4 from 14,15-diHETE is described.

title: Structures of the Human GTPase MMAA and Vitamin B12-dependent Methylmalonyl-CoA Mutase and Insight into Their Complex Formation
finding: Crystal structures of human MMAA with GDP (2.5 A; a GMPPNP co-crystallisation also gave GDP) and of human methylmalonyl-CoA mutase as apo (2.60 A) and with AdoCbl (1.95 A), using N-terminally truncated recombinant constructs. Dimeric assembly differs from the bacterial proteins. MMAA is a weak GTPase (Km 1210 +/- 330 uM, kcat 0.030 per min) stimulated by apo mutase (Km 74 uM, kcat 0.15 per min) and less by holo mutase (8-fold). A stable complex needed GMPPNP rather than GDP and the apoenzyme (size-exclusion; co-elution data not shown), and it was abolished by the patient mutation G188R, which keeps basal GTPase activity. The gatekeeping and release model is speculative.
locator: Results: Structure of Nucleotide-bound hMMAA; Homodimeric Assembly of hMUT; hMMAA Is a P-loop GTPase Modulated by hMUT, Table 2; Physical Interaction of hMMAA-hMUT, Fig. 5

title: Differences in the Serum Nonesterified Fatty Acid Profile of Young Women Associated with a Recent History of Gestational Diabetes and Overweight/Obesity
finding: LC-MS/MS quantification of 41 serum NEFA species in fasting sera of 111 young women (62 post-gestational diabetes, 49 controls) gave group median molar percentages of 25.1 and 25.6 for 16:0, 39.5 and 39.1 for 18:1, 11.1 and 10.4 for 18:2 and 8.5 and 9.0 for 18:0, with trace species quantified down to 0.050 percent for 19:0, 0.005 percent for 24:6 and 0.006 percent for 26:1.
locator: Results: Serum NEFA composition in women after GDM and controls; Table 3

title: A bacterial light response reveals an orphan desaturase for human plasmalogen synthesis
finding: In Myxococcus xanthus the gene carF appears to encode the ether lipid desaturase that forms the plasmalogen vinyl ether bond (assignment from knockout and rescue; an in vitro test with a deletion-strain extract gave only a small peak). The human homolog TMEM189 and other animal homologs could functionally replace CarF in M. xanthus. Knockout of TMEM189 in a human cell line eliminated plasmalogens (measured as dimethylacetal peaks, three biological replicates). The name PEDS1 does not appear in the text.
locator: Results: Fig. 2 (A, C), Fig. 3 (B to E), Fig. 4 (A, B); Abstract

title: Navigating the B12 Road: Assimilation, Delivery, and Disorders of Cobalamin
finding: Minireview of mammalian cobalamin uptake, lysosomal release, cytosolic processing by CblC and delivery to methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase. In its closing Summary the review lists the mitochondrial membrane transporters that bring cobalamin into the mitochondrion as not yet identified (as is the reductase partner of ATR), and the Figure 2 model marks this transporter with a question mark.

title: A randomized comparison between rasburicase and allopurinol in children with lymphoma or leukemia at high risk for tumor lysis
finding: Open-label, randomised, multicentre trial of rasburicase (recombinant urate oxidase) versus oral allopurinol in 52 children with leukaemia or lymphoma. The mean plasma uric acid area under the curve over 96 hours was 128 +/- 70 mg/dL.h with rasburicase and 329 +/- 129 with allopurinol (P < .0001; intent-to-treat, last value carried forward), and uric acid fell 86.0% against 12.1% at 4 hours (secondary end point). Rasburicase patients presented with somewhat higher uric acid (not significant). The study was too small to compare renal outcome. Intravenous allopurinol was not available for comparison. Industry-supported. Humans lack endogenous urate oxidase because of a nonsense mutation.
locator: Results: Control of plasma uric acid, Table 2, Fig. 2, Fig. 3; Materials and methods; Discussion

title: Methylation of tRNAAsp by the DNA Methyltransferase Homolog Dnmt2
finding: Human DNMT2 showed no DNA methylation (Fig. 3A). It methylated a small RNA only when the RNA came from Dnmt2-deficient tissue. In mouse that RNA was identified by tandem mass spectrometry as tRNA-Asp, methylated at cytosine 38 of the anticodon loop. Purified human DNMT2 methylated RNAs of about 80 nucleotides from Dnmt2-deficient mouse, Drosophila and Arabidopsis; mass spectrometry identifies tRNA-Asp for mouse only. Unmodified in vitro transcribed tRNA-Asp was not a substrate, so methylation is probably guided by other modifications (mannosylqueuosine is proposed). The fly DNA test used the fly enzyme. Dnmt2 mutants were viable and fertile.
locator: Results: Fig. 3 (A and B), Fig. 4 (A to D)

title: Coordination Chemistry Controls Coenzyme B12 Synthesis by Human Adenosine Triphosphate:Cob(I)alamin Adenosyltransferase
finding: In vitro, NADPH with FDXR and FDX1 (adrenodoxin) reduces MMAB-bound cob(II)alamin and supports adenosylcobalamin synthesis (kcat 4.7 min-1, 2.5-fold below titanium(III) citrate; Km for FDX1 135 nM), and no AdoCbl forms without FDX1 or FDXR. The 4-coordinate cob(II)alamin reduction potential is -325 ± 9 mV (measured on the R190H variant); the authors call FDX1 a potential MMAB redox partner.

title: Coordination Chemistry Controls Coenzyme B12 Synthesis by Human Adenosine Triphosphate:Cob(I)alamin Adenosyltransferase
finding: In the introduction, cited as prior work rather than tested here, methionine synthase reductase (MTRR) is described as able to supply electrons for AdoCbl synthesis in vitro, while being a cytoplasmic protein with no known effect of its deficiency on mitochondrial cobalamin metabolism. The paper's own measurements give a reduction potential of -325 +/- 9 mV for four-coordinate cob(II)alamin bound to human MMAB and identify the mitochondrial ferredoxin adrenodoxin (FDX1) as an electron donor that supports NADPH-dependent AdoCbl synthesis.

title: Strict Regiospecificity of Human Epithelial 15-Lipoxygenase-2 Delineates Its Transcellular Synthesis Potential
finding: Purified recombinant human 15-lipoxygenase-2 (ALOX15B) oxygenated both 5-HPETE and 5-HETE at C15 to 5,15-diH(P)ETE, with catalytic efficiencies of 31% and 25% of that for arachidonate, while 12-HPETE and 15-HPETE were not substrates and 5,15-diHPETE was not converted further to lipoxins. All measurements are in vitro with the purified enzyme.
locator: Results and Discussion: Steady-State Kinetics of 5-HPETE and Formation of the Lipoxin Intermediate 5,15-diHPETE; Table 1

title: Measurement of allantoin and uric acid in human body fluids. A potential index of free-radical reactions in vivo?
finding: Methods are described for measuring uric acid and allantoin in human body fluids, with concentrations in serum and synovial fluid. Serum allantoin of healthy volunteers was 14.1 to 25.4 uM. In rheumatoid patients serum uric acid was not significantly changed while allantoin was raised. The authors suggest that allantoin may index free-radical reactions in vivo, and also state that raised allantoin does not prove increased radical formation. That radical attack on uric acid yields allantoin is cited from earlier work (ref. 1) and was not shown here. Small numbers of samples, controls not age-matched, synovial fluid only from knee joints of rheumatoid patients. The scan is partly illegible (Table 1 and the abstract).
locator: Discussion; Table 1; Results: Analysis of allantoin

title: Generation and analysis of context-specific genome-scale metabolic models derived from single-cell RNA-Seq data
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: ftINIT builds context-specific models from pooled single-cell or bulk RNA-seq; with the mask used in this study, reactions without gene rules (spontaneous, exchange, transport and 52 custom reactions for protein generation and metabolite pooling) are left out of the optimization and always kept in the final model, except in the Metabolic Atlas models.

title: Crystallographic and Kinetic Studies of Human Mitochondrial Acetoacetyl-CoA Thiolase: The Importance of Potassium and Chloride Ions for Its Structure and Function,
finding: Human mitochondrial acetoacetyl-CoA thiolase (T2) degrades acetoacetyl-CoA and 2-methylacetoacetyl-CoA with similar catalytic efficiencies. Turnover numbers rise about 3-fold with 40 mM KCl (Table 2 compares KCl with NaCl at 40 mM; Km of 2-methylacetoacetyl-CoA is not affected by potassium). Crystal structures are reported for the apo and CoA forms with and without potassium; the potassium site is near the CoA site and the catalytic site, T2 has weak affinity for potassium, and a high-affinity chloride site was also found. The Phe325-Pro326 dipeptide is proposed to determine the 2-methyl-branched specificity from the structure and a docked model (not a crystal structure with that substrate); the authors say chiral specificity is not established.
locator: Results: Kinetic Data, Table 2; Potassium Ion Binding Site; Catalytic Properties

title: Dnmt3L cooperates with the Dnmt3 family of de novo DNA methyltransferases to establish maternal imprints in mice
finding: Dnmt3L, a Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b homolog without methyltransferase activity, is required in mice for establishing maternal methylation imprints and for correct expression of maternally imprinted genes; it interacts with Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b and co-localizes with them in transfected cell nuclei, and Dnmt3a-/- Dnmt3b+/- mice show the same failure of maternal imprinting. Dnmt3a and Dnmt3L are also required for spermatogenesis.

title: The Human Dnmt2 Has Residual DNA-(Cytosine-C5) Methyltransferase Activity
finding: Purified recombinant human Dnmt2 (from E. coli) showed weak DNA methyltransferase activity in two independent in vitro assays, which explains earlier failures to detect it; other assays found none. Bisulfite sequencing of 44 clones of a single 558-mer fragment (34 CG sites) showed preferential methylation at CG with a loose ttnCGga(g/a) consensus that the authors call tentative because few sites were analysed. An active-site variant kept some activity (more than 10-fold lower). No covalent complex with DNA was detected (data not shown). The authors suggest a more specialised role in vivo.
locator: Results: HPLC/TLC Activity Assay; Bisulfite Sequencing Activity Assay, Tables I and II; Fig. 5

title: Photosynthesis of Previtamin D3 in Human Skin and the Physiologic Consequences
finding: In surgically obtained hypopigmented Caucasian skin, radiation in the 290 to 320 nm band converted 7-dehydrocholesterol into previtamin D3 across all epidermal strata and, to a lesser degree, the dermis, with the highest previtamin D3 content in stratum spinosum and stratum basale (Table 1). Previtamin D3 then rearranged into vitamin D3 by a temperature-driven, non-photochemical step (half-conversion at 28 h and 83 percent at equilibrium after 4 days at 37 C in methanol in vitro, half-conversion in 18 h and a 95:5 ratio by day 3 in rat skin in vivo); the authors argue against catalysis because incubations of previtamin D3 with plasma or skin homogenates followed the same time course as in methanol, and they attribute the faster in vivo rate to removal of vitamin D3 by the vitamin D-binding protein.
locator: Results and discussion paragraphs on cutaneous sites and thermal equilibration (Table 1; Fig. 1B; Fig. 2 scheme)

title: A general introduction to the biochemistry of mitochondrial fatty acid β‐oxidation
finding: Review of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation: long-chain acyl-CoAs are handled by the membrane-bound VLCAD (ACADVL) and the trifunctional protein (HADHA and HADHB), which carries hydratase, long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and thiolase activities, while medium- and short-chain intermediates are processed in the matrix by a separate set of soluble enzymes, crotonase (ECHS1), M/SCHAD (HADH) and MCKAT (ACAA2), all with broad specificity up to about ten carbons. Auxiliary enzymes are needed for unsaturated substrates, the enoyl-CoA isomerase (given as DCI, now ECI1) and DECR1.
locator: Biochemical basis of fatty acid oxidation: The beta-oxidation cycle; Fig. 1

title: Characterization of four mammalian 3‐hydroxyacyl‐CoA dehydratases involved in very long‐chain fatty acid synthesis
finding: In vitro assays with proteins from transfected HeLa cells showed that all four human HACD proteins converted 3-hydroxypalmitoyl-CoA to the 2,3-enoyl product. In the yeast PHS1 shut-off strain only HACD1 and HACD2 restored growth; HACD3 and HACD4 did not, which the authors do not take as excluding activity because ectopic proteins are often unstable in yeast. Only 3-hydroxypalmitoyl-CoA was tested, so substrate preferences are open, and no polyunsaturated substrate was used. HACD3 mRNA was found in most tissues examined by Northern blot; HACD1 and HACD2 patterns come from earlier work. Co-immunoprecipitation in HEK 293T cells showed that HACD proteins can interact with ELOVL1 to ELOVL7, with some preferences.
locator: Results: 3.1 with Fig. 2A and Fig. 3; 3.2 with Fig. 4; 3.3 with Fig. 5

title: SLC22A5 (OCTN2) Carnitine Transporter—Indispensable for Cell Metabolism, a Jekyll and Hyde of Human Cancer
finding: This review states that of the three plasma-membrane carnitine transporters, SLC22A5 (OCTN2) is the only high-affinity one that is ubiquitously expressed (Km 4.34 micromolar), SLC22A16 (CT2) also has high affinity (Km 20.3 micromolar) but is expressed mainly in testis and epididymis, and SLC6A14 transports carnitine with low affinity (Km 830 micromolar).

title: Fat-1 mice convert n-6 to n-3 fatty acids
finding: Transgenic mice carrying the C. elegans fat-1 n-3 desaturase had more n-3 and less n-6 fatty acids, so that the n-6 to n-3 ratio fell from 20 to 50 to almost 1, in all organs and tissues tested (Table 1). Skeletal muscle has more EPA than DHA, while DHA dominates in other organs. Wild-type and transgenic 8-week-old females were fed the same diet, high in n-6 and low in n-3 (the main text says deficient), so the result is not on an n-3-free diet. The milk sample was stomach content of 5-day-old pups. Four generations were examined. The authors state that mammals cannot make n-3 from n-6. A corrigendum states that the first author is an inventor on a related patent application.

title: The genomes of the South American opossum (Monodelphis domestica) and platypus (Ornithorhynchus anatinus) encode a more complete purine catabolic pathway than placental mammals
journal: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part D: Genomics and Proteomics
finding: Genome searches in opossum (Monodelphis domestica) and platypus (Ornithorhynchus anatinus), compared with 15 other vertebrates, found all six purine catabolic genes examined (XDH, UOX, 5-hydroxyisourate hydrolase, OHCU decarboxylase, allantoinase and allantoicase), including the allantoinase gene that is absent from placental mammal genomes; Ka/Ks values of 0.07 to 0.47 are consistent with purifying selection on all six. No allantoinase remnant was found at the expected syntenic position in placental genomes, so the loss is specific to placental mammals.
locator: Results: The opossum and platypus genomes encode a more complete set of genes for purine catabolism than do placental mammals; Fig. 2 and Table 1

title: The Evolutionary Fate of the Genes Encoding the Purine Catabolic Enzymes in Hominoids, Birds, and Reptiles
finding: Comparative genomics of five hominoids, two birds and one lizard. In hominoids, HIU hydrolase has inactivating mutations in human, chimpanzee and gibbon but not in gorilla and orangutan; OHCU decarboxylase has them only in gibbon, and the calls for the other four rest on Ka/Ks alone and are provisional. The authors say the loss of UOX likely triggered the deterioration of these genes and also that the evidence is mixed. In birds and lizard UOX has no inactivating mutation and Ka/Ks 0.26; HIU hydrolase is retained in all three, ALLN and ALLC only in the lizard, and OHCU decarboxylase was not detected in any. No protein or enzyme data for the retained genes. Retention through a function outside purine catabolism is the authors' hypothesis.
locator: Results: Predicted Fate of the Hominoid and Bird/Reptile Purine Catabolic Genes; Fig. 2, Tables 1-2

title: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy: Very long-chain fatty acid metabolism, ABC half-transporters and the complicated route to treatment
finding: Review. The authors state that X-ALD is caused by mutations in ABCD1, encoding the peroxisomal half-transporter ALDP, and that ALDP mutations raise very-long-chain fatty acid levels and reduce their peroxisomal beta-oxidation (cited from earlier work). They report, citing other groups, that overexpression of ALDRP corrected the defect in patient fibroblasts and gave normal VLCFA levels in spinal cord, sciatic nerve and adrenal gland of Abcd1 knockout mice carrying an ALDRP transgene; PMP70 corrected only partly. The function of ALDP and its main transported metabolite are unresolved. Treatment is called a possibility; a 4-PBA trial did not raise ALDRP in white blood cells.
locator: Sections: ABCD1, the gene mutated in X-ALD, and its protein product ALDP; Redundant function of ALDP, ALDRP and PMP70

title: The crystal structure of human mitochondrial 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase (T1): insight into the reaction mechanism of its thiolase and thioesterase activities
journal: Acta Crystallographica Section D Biological Crystallography
finding: Crystal structures of human mitochondrial 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase T1 (UniProt P42765), apo and with CoA, were solved at 2.0 A with a tetramer as the biological unit; in the CoA structure the catalytic Cys92 is oxidised to hydroxycysteine. In solution T1 has low acyl-CoA thioesterase activity, highest with butyryl-CoA, which needs reduced DTT; the mechanism is not established because the acylated cysteine could not be captured. It is a competent biosynthetic thiolase with Km and kcat similar to T2. Section 3.9 notes, citing earlier work (Middleton and Bartlett 1983), that the liver contains significant T1, which apparently compensates for T2 deficiency in the synthesis of ketone bodies; that the T1 of this paper supports ketone body synthesis is a hypothesis, using a mitochondrial acetyl-CoA concentration cited from earlier work. Recombinant protein with a His tag.
locator: Sections: 3.1 with Table 2; 3.2 and 3.3 with Table 1; 3.7 with Fig. 7; 3.9

title: Decyanation of vitamin B12 by a trafficking chaperone
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Purified human MMACHC with bound cyanocobalamin was converted to cob(II)alamin on addition of NADPH and either methionine synthase reductase or NR1, both diflavin oxidoreductases (kobs about 0.10 and 0.068 per min). Free cyanocobalamin was not reduced by these reductases without MMACHC. EPR identified the product as base-off cob(II)alamin. Methyl- and adenosylcobalamin bound to MMACHC were not reduced (data not shown), and 1 mM glutathione had no effect (data not shown). Release of cyanide by reductive elimination is the authors' interpretation. Assimilation of cob(II)alamin into the active cofactors is cited as known and was not tested. The cblC fibroblast observations come from earlier work. The function of NR1 is not known. In vitro only.
locator: Results and Discussion: MMACHC Catalyzes the Decyanation of CNCbl; Fig. 4

title: MeaB Is a Component of the Methylmalonyl-CoA Mutase Complex Required for Protection of the Enzyme from Inactivation
finding: In Methylobacterium extorquens AM1 meaB and meaD mutants lose growth on C1 and C2 compounds. The meaB mutant has inactive mutase that is not due to lack of AdoCbl. Extracts of the double mutants (epm meaB, meaD meaB) had low mutase activity only when AdoCbl was added; no activity without it. Purified MeaB formed a complex with the mutase (non-denaturing PAGE) and raised its activity in vitro (3.9 units per mg with MeaB). The authors suggest MeaB protects the mutase from suicide inactivation; the role of GTP hydrolysis is unknown, and MeaB is not a reactivating factor under the conditions tested.
locator: Results: MCM Activity in M. extorquens Mutants Defective in MeaB and MeaD, Table I; Double mutants; Complex Formation, Fig. 4 and Fig. 5; MeaB Increases MCM Activity in Vitro

title: Hepatic synthesis of carnitine from protein-bound trimethyl-lysine. Lysosomal digestion of methyl-lysine-labelled asialo-fetuin
finding: Rat liver took up lysine-methylated asialo-fetuin from the blood almost completely. Of the protein-bound trimethyl-lysine at least 34.6% (abstract; 34.7% in the discussion) was converted to carnitine in 3 h in vivo, and 30% in 90 min in an isolated perfused liver (abstract). The in vivo value is a minimum: extraction efficiency was unknown and no correction was made for losses. The 3 h in vivo experiment shown in the figure legend used a single 165 g rat. After injection of the mono- and dimethyl-lysine derivative no radioactivity was found in the carnitine fractions (under 200 d.p.m., 0.2% of the sample). The amino acids released from lysosomes were further metabolised in the cytosol (abstract).
locator: Abstract; Results: tables on carnitine in liver and carcass; perfused liver; Discussion

title: Identification of the Human and Bovine ATP:Cob(I)alamin Adenosyltransferase cDNAs Based on Complementation of a Bacterial Mutant
finding: The bovine ATP:cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase cDNA was found by complementing a bacterial ATR-deficient strain; about 250,000 human cDNAs gave no positives, and the human cDNA was found through the bovine sequence. The bovine clone lacked part of its 5' end. In E. coli expression strains activities were 85.7 (bovine) and 98 (human) nmol/min/mg in the best fractions (87 and 98 in the abstract). The human cDNA complemented the bacterial ATR mutant. ATR protein was altered on western blots of three cblB patient fibroblast lines (run twice). The authors propose that the gene corresponds to the cblB group; no mutation data for the patient lines are given.

title: Human ATP:Cob(I)alamin Adenosyltransferase and Its Interaction with Methionine Synthase Reductase
finding: Recombinant human ATR (MMAB) variants 239K and 239M, expressed in E. coli without targeting sequences or tags, had specific activities of 220 and 190 nmol per min per mg and Km values of 6.3 and 6.9 uM for ATP and 1.2 and 1.6 uM for cob(I)alamin (assayed with titanium(III) citrate). In a reconstituted system methionine synthase reductase, with ATR, supported AdoCbl synthesis; since ATR needs cob(I)alamin the authors infer reductase action. ATR increased cob(I)alamin production by the reductase, taken as physical interaction; 35% of the cob(I)alamin was trapped. Only 239K was tested in this system, and reduction can occur independently of MSR in vivo.

title: Cloning of a human cDNA encoding a novel enzyme involved in the elongation of long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids
finding: A human liver cDNA named HELO1 (897 bp, 299 residues, with a histidine box) was expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. With 25 uM of fatty acid added to the medium, it elongated 18:3n-6 to 20:3n-6, 20:4n-6 to 22:4n-6, 18:4n-3 to 20:4n-3, 20:5n-3 to 22:5n-3 and 18:3n-3 to 20:3n-3, with conversions of about 30% to 80%. It also elongated endogenous monounsaturated fatty acids, so its specificity is broad. No C24 product from 22:4n-6 or 22:5n-3 was seen. Docosahexaenoic acid is not tested as a substrate. mRNA was highest in testis and adrenal gland among 22 tissues, with brain, lung and prostate lower. Yeast host only. The gene symbol ELOVL5 does not appear in the paper.
locator: Results: Expression of the human cDNAs in yeast; Fig. 3, Fig. 4. Results: HELO1 mRNA distribution in human tissues; Fig. 5

title: Identification and expression of mammalian long‐chain PUFA elongation enzymes
finding: Human ELOVL2 (888 bp, 296 residues) and mouse Elovl2 (876 bp, 292 residues) were expressed in Saccharomyces cerevisiae with 25 uM substrate. Both elongated 20:4n-6 to 22:4n-6, 22:4n-6 to 24:4n-6, 20:5n-3 to 22:5n-3 and 22:5n-3 to 24:5n-3, with small conversions (for example 3.29% and 1.18% for 20:4n-6). Unlike the mouse enzyme, the human enzyme did not act on C18 PUFA. Only mouse Elovl2 was tested in mouse L cells (100 uM substrates); with 20:4n-6, 24:4n-6 rose from 0.59% to 3.01%. L cells elongate these substrates themselves, and the effect is an increase over that.
locator: Results: Expression of the mouse and human cDNA in yeast, Tables 1 and 2; Expression of the mouse cDNA in mouse L cells, Tables 3 and 4

title: Glutathione-dependent One-electron Transfer Reactions Catalyzed by a B12 Trafficking Protein
finding: Purified human CblC (residues 1-244) with bound cyanocobalamin was decyanated by 8 mM glutathione at 37 C to cob(II)alamin, efficiently only under anaerobic conditions; under air decyanation was slight. Aquacobalamin bound to human CblC was reduced to cob(II)alamin by glutathione anaerobically (kobs 0.36 per min); under air no stable cob(II)alamin formed. C. elegans CblC did both reactions, with similar rates under air and anaerobically. Other thiols also supported decyanation. Purified proteins and cobalamins only; the authors call the physiological relevance possible.
locator: Results: Thiol-dependent Decyanation of CNCbl by hCblC; Fig. 4. Results: Reduction of CblC-bound OH2Cbl by Thiols; Fig. 6

title: Structure of the human signal peptidase complex reveals the determinants for signal peptide cleavage
finding: Cryo-EM at about 4.9 A resolution plus structural proteomics gave structures of two paralogous forms of the human signal peptidase complex, differing in the proteolytic subunit (SEC11A or SEC11C); the maps of the two are virtually indistinguishable, and no functional difference between them was established. The catalytic triad Ser56/68, His96/108 and Asp122/134 is assigned from mutagenesis and positioning, not from resolved side chains (Asp is called best positioned). The active site abuts a transmembrane window that thins the bilayer (micelle about 23 A against 35 to 40 A outside; 26% average thinning in simulation). Coarse-grained simulations with model leucine peptides of SPC-C indicate specificity by hydrophobic-segment length, together with limited shape complementarity; the authors say this is likely and needs a substrate-bound structure. In vitro cleavage was tested with one substrate and was partial.
locator: Results: Human SPC exists in two paralogs, Fig. 1; SPC architecture and topology, Fig. 2, Table 1; Characterization of SEC11 and the SP c-region binding pocket, Fig. 4A-C; The SPC induces membrane thinning, Figs. 4D-H and 5; Membrane thinning ensures selectivity of the SPC, Fig. 6

title: Knockout of Tmlhe in mice is not associated with autism spectrum disorder phenotypes or motor dysfunction despite low carnitine levels
finding: Mice with constitutive inactivation of the Tmlhe-encoded trimethyllysine dioxygenase had carnitine reduced by more than 90% against wild type, together with very low gamma-butyrobetaine, yet showed no autism-associated social, cognitive or repetitive-behaviour changes, unchanged muscle strength and coordination, and a life expectancy similar to wild type.

title: The Biosynthesis of A2E, a Fluorophore of Aging Retina, Involves the Formation of the Precursor, A2-PE, in the Photoreceptor Outer Segment Membrane
finding: All-trans-retinal and dipalmitoyl-phosphatidylethanolamine reacted without an enzyme in chloroform at 37 C (up to 3 days, retinal in excess, much slower at room temperature) to give A2-PE, identified by UV (456 and 337 nm) and mass spectrometry. A2-PE was also detected in bovine rod outer segments with excess retinal and in degenerating retinas of RCS rats, not in normal retinas. Streptomyces phospholipase D released A2E from A2-PE, so the authors call A2-PE the likely A2E precursor. A2E itself was not detected in RCS retina, and the site of A2E generation is not established.
locator: Results: Identification of Reference DP-NRPE and DP-A2-PE, Figs. 2 and 3; Hydrolysis of A2-PE, Fig. 8; Detection in Rat Retinal Tissues, Figs. 4C and 7A

title: Carnitine transport and fatty acid oxidation
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Cell Research
finding: Review: normal circulating carnitine is 25-50 µM (0-8 µM in primary carnitine deficiency); cells accumulate carnitine and kidneys reabsorb it through the high-affinity carnitine transporter OCTN2 (SLC22A5), and inborn errors of carnitine synthesis usually leave plasma carnitine normal.

title: Double Bond Removal from Odd-numbered Carbons during Peroxisomal β-Oxidation of Arachidonic Acid Requires both 2,4-Dienoyl-CoA Reductase and Δ3,5,Δ2,4-Dienoyl-CoA Isomerase
finding: Incubating clofibrate-induced rat liver peroxisomes with [1-14C]4,7,10-hexadecatrienoate gave 2-trans-4,7,10-hexadecatetraenoate plus two isomers carrying a conjugated triene (UV maxima at 257, 267 and 277 nm) that the authors assign as 3,5,7,10-hexadecatetraenoate, and the matching accumulation of 2-trans-4,8,11,14-eicosapentaenoate from arachidonate without NADPH led them to conclude that removal of the odd-numbered double bonds of arachidonate needs NADPH-dependent 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase together with a delta-3,5,delta-2,4-dienoyl-CoA isomerase acting in the reverse direction.
locator: Results (Fig. 2 radiochromatograms, Figs. 4 and 5 UV spectra) and Discussion with the proposed pathway (Fig. 8)

title: Structural basis of signal peptide recognition by the signal peptidase complex
finding: A 2.6 Angstrom cryo-EM map of human SPC-A bound to a model signal peptide shows the c-region of the peptide in a hydrophobic luminal groove next to the active site, a narrow gate at the transition from c-region to h-region, and the h-region in a transmembrane window; substrate binding stabilises the N- and C-terminal helices of SEC11A that are unresolved in the apo structure. Molecular dynamics and AlphaFold modelling support this binding mode.

title: Integration of clinical data with a genome‐scale metabolic model of the human adipocyte
finding: iAdipocytes1809 builds its lipid pool reactions from published fatty acid compositions, with plasma non-esterified fatty acids from a fasting human plasma lipidomics study that reported 31 fatty acids; fatty acids absent from that study were assigned half the lowest reported concentration. In Supplementary Dataset 8 the plasma NEFA column lists 59 fatty acids, 31 with measured values summing to 214.3 nmol/ml and the other 28 marked as not reported and given the normalised value 9e-6.

title: Genome-scale metabolic modelling of hepatocytes reveals serine deficiency in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
finding: HMR 2.0 (8,181 reactions, 6,007 metabolites, 3,765 genes) extends lipid metabolism with 59 individual fatty acids in place of a generic fatty acid pool, and the hepatocyte model iHepatocytes2322 built from it (7,930 reactions, 2,322 genes) uses the same 59 fatty acids.

title: Architecture of the human G-protein-methylmalonyl-CoA mutase nanoassembly for B12 delivery and repair
finding: A crystal structure of the human MMUT-MMAA assembly (two MMUT chains with two MMAA dimers) shows the MMUT B12 domain rotated about 180 degrees relative to free MMUT and exposed to solvent, with MMAA wedged between the substrate and B12 domains and the interconnecting belt partially disordered. Methylmalonic aciduria mutations at the interfaces (MMUT R228Q, R616C, R694W; MMAA R98G, R209S) reduce MMUT-stimulated GTPase activation and MMAA-gated AdoCbl transfer, supporting the relevance of the structure.
locator: Results: MMUT in the M2C2 complex; Fig. 3A

title: Identification of ABC transporters acting in vitamin B 12 metabolism in Caenorhabditis elegans
finding: Of 37 C. elegans ABC transporter mutants screened for methylmalonic acid excretion, the wht-6 deletion mutant excreted about 11 times more than wild type and incorporated about 35% as much [14C]propionate (mrp-1 and mrp-2 mutants also did). Cystathionine excretion was similar to wild type, but the cystathionine results complicated the authors' interpretation. B12 in the medium modestly lowered MMA excretion (2.3 uM, p < 0.05). The authors propose wht-6 as a candidate mitochondrial cobalamin importer. They name no specific human ortholog among the five ABCG members, state that no direct evidence for mitochondrial location or transport exists, and note that most of the independent point mutants were at wild-type level.

title: Urate as a Physiological Substrate for Myeloperoxidase
finding: Purified myeloperoxidase with hydrogen peroxide oxidised urate to 5-hydroxyisourate, which decayed mainly to allantoin (over 50% of the urate oxidised). Rate constants of urate with compound I and compound II were 4.6e5 and 1.7e4 per molar per second (pH 7.0, 25 C, buffer). Urate and chloride compete, but at normal plasma concentrations hypochlorous acid is the main product and urate a minor substrate (about 3% of compound I). Neutrophils stimulated with PMA and cytochalasin B in 75% plasma made allantoin, and inhibitors showed dependence on NADPH oxidase, MPO and superoxide. The plasma experiment is ex vivo and MPO dependence rests on inhibitors.
locator: Results: Spectral Changes of MPO and Rate Constants; Fig. 2C, Fig. 3C. Results: Production of Allantoin by Neutrophils in Plasma; Fig. 8

title: Lecithin Retinol Acyltransferase Contains Cysteine Residues Essential for Catalysis
finding: Cysteine mutants of recombinant human LRAT expressed in HEK-293T membranes, with activity normalised to expression. C161A and C168A were virtually inactive (C168A and the double mutant are data not shown). C182A and C208A were at least as active as wild type. C161S kept a few percent of wild-type activity with a pH-rate profile that is not readily interpretable, while C168S was substantially active. The authors conclude LRAT is a thiol acyltransferase and hypothesise C161 as the nucleophile; they also raise a binding-only role for C161S. Sensitivity to thiol reagents is taken from earlier work, and supporting affinity-label data are unpublished.
locator: Results: Kinetic Studies on LRAT and the C161, C168, C182 and C208 mutants; Table 2; Figures 2-5; Discussion

title: Identification of Two Mammalian Reductases Involved in the Two-carbon Fatty Acyl Elongation Cascade
finding: Two human reductases of the microsomal fatty acyl elongation cycle were identified: KAR (3-ketoacyl-CoA reductase) and TER (trans-2,3-enoyl-CoA reductase). Each acted on long and very long chain substrates; 'respectively' in the paper refers to the reactions, not to chain-length classes. Evidence is overexpression with the elongase LCE and RNAi in cultured cells; knockdown was partial (final elongated product down 40 to 50% with KAR RNAi). Mouse orthologue results are data not shown. Essentiality in vivo needs knockout mice, and other reductases may contribute. TER inhibition did not preclude a role in the dehydratase step. The paper uses the names KAR and TER and GenBank NM_016142, not the gene symbols HSD17B12 and TECR.
locator: Results: Figs. 5-7 (overexpression with LCE; RNAi of KAR and TER); Discussion

title: In vitro construction of the COQ metabolon unveils the molecular determinants of coenzyme Q biosynthesis
finding: Using ancestral sequence reconstruction to obtain soluble enzymes, the authors assembled the animal COQ biosynthetic pathway in vitro, assigned enzymes to steps that had been uncharacterised, and showed that the kinase COQ8 increases and streamlines coenzyme Q production in that reconstituted system.

title: Loss of Urate Oxidase Activity in Hominoids and its Evolutionary Implications
finding: Urate oxidase (Uox) sequences from five hominoids, three Old World monkeys and one New World monkey. The inactivation in the human and great ape clade results from a single CGA to TGA nonsense mutation in exon 2. The gibbon lineage has an independent nonsense mutation at a different CGA codon in exon 2, or alternatively a one-base deletion in exon 3 or a one-base insertion in exon 5; the authors could not decide among them and reject the earlier 13-bp deletion claim. Substitutions in the CAAT box or cis-acting element of functional primate genes may lower transcription (hedged, no expression data). The authors describe a two-step deterioration, promoter first and then coding region.

title: ELOVL1 production of C24 acyl-CoAs is linked to C24 sphingolipid synthesis
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Membranes of HEK293T cells overexpressing each human ELOVL1-7 were assayed with [14C]malonyl-CoA and 11 acyl-CoAs (C16:0 to C26:0, C18 PUFAs, 20:4n-6): ELOVL1 elongated saturated C18:0-C26:0 (highest on C22:0) and none of the unsaturated substrates tested; ELOVL2 and ELOVL5 acted only on PUFA (most active on 20:4n-6 and 18:3n-6); ELOVL4 weakly on C24:0 and C26:0. No C22 PUFA was tested.

title: Dnmt2 is not required for de novo and maintenance methylation of viral DNA in embryonic stem cells
finding: Mouse Dnmt2 was cloned as a homolog of fission yeast pmt1 and has all the conserved methyltransferase motifs. No methyltransferase activity was detected so far in baculovirus- or bacteria-expressed protein, with poly(dI-dC) or lambda phage DNA as substrate (data not shown), and the authors do not know why. ES cells with a putative null allele (exons for the putative catalytic PPC motif deleted) methylated endogenous virus DNA and newly integrated provirus (scored 2 to 4 days after infection) like wild type. The assay reads HpaII/MspI sites only. The authors conclude Dnmt2 is not essential for global de novo or maintenance methylation in ES cells, and list other possibilities: a few specific targets, non-CpG sites, compensation by Dnmt1, or no function as a cytosine methyltransferase.

title: A G-protein editor gates coenzyme B12 loading and is corrupted in methylmalonic aciduria
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Purified bacterial proteins from Methylobacterium extorquens AM1 (MeaB, adenosyltransferase, methylmalonyl-CoA mutase). MeaB uses the energy of GTP hydrolysis to gate transfer of adenosylcobalamin from the transferase to the mutase. GTP binding is enough for the editing of cofactor forms. The patient mutation R616C of the human mutase was mimicked as R585C in the bacterial enzyme: its own activity with added adenosylcobalamin was normal, but MeaB failed to protect it from reconstitution with cob(II)alamin. The mutation also lowers affinity for MeaB and GTPase stimulation. The accumulation of inactive enzyme is the authors' model and was not measured in patient cells. In vitro, bacterial proteins only; the human mutation was not tested.

title: Mechanistic Details of Early Steps in Coenzyme Q Biosynthesis Pathway in Yeast
finding: In S. cerevisiae Hfd1 oxidises 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde to 4-hydroxybenzoate for coenzyme Q synthesis. Q was 7-fold lower in cells lacking HFD1, restored by 4-hydroxybenzoate but not by tyrosine. Human ALDH3A1 raised Q in those cells when 4-hydroxybenzaldehyde was added to the medium; ALDH3A2 and ALDH3B1 did not restore Q synthesis. How the side chain of 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate is shortened is unresolved, so the pathway is partial. The authors suggest a similar pathway in animals and call this the first stage of testing conservation.

title: COQ4 is required for the oxidative decarboxylation of the C1 carbon of coenzyme Q in eukaryotic cells
finding: COQ4 catalyses the C1 decarboxylation and hydroxylation of CoQ precursors as one oxidative decarboxylation: COQ4-knockout HEK293 cells make no CoQ10 and accumulate the COQ2 product 3-decaprenyl-4-hydroxybenzoate, COQ4 complements an E. coli strain lacking these steps, and COQ4 forms polyprenyl-benzoquinone in C. glutamicum. No in vitro assay with purified COQ4 is reported.

title: Role of Human 15-Lipoxygenase-2 in the Biosynthesis of the Lipoxin Intermediate, 5S,15S-diHpETE, Implicated with the Altered Positional Specificity of Human 15-Lipoxygenase-1
finding: With purified recombinant human lipoxygenases, oxygenation of 12S-HETE and 15S-HETE by 5-lipoxygenase was kinetically slow, so the authors conclude that 5S-HETE is the first intermediate in the in vitro biosynthesis of both 5S,12S-diHETE and 5S,15S-diHETE. 15-lipoxygenase-1 acting on 5S-HETE gave 90 percent 5S,12S-diHETE with kinetics 5-fold greater than 12-lipoxygenase, while 15-lipoxygenase-2 gave 5S,15S-diHETE with a kcat/Km flux twice that of 15-lipoxygenase-1.

title: The suppression of 5-lipoxygenation of arachidonic acid in human polymorphonuclear leucocytes by the 15-lipoxygenase product (15S)-hydroxy-(5Z,8Z,11Z,13E)-eicosatetraenoic acid: structure-activity relationship and mechanism of action
finding: In human polymorphonuclear leucocytes, labelled 15-HETE was converted to a compound that co-eluted with authentic 5,15-diHETE and had a UV maximum at 244 nm; 5,15-diHETE formation was strongly stimulated by hydroperoxy fatty acids or arachidonic acid. Human recombinant 5-lipoxygenase used 15-HETE as a substrate with an efficiency comparable to arachidonic acid (assay of 50 s at 4 C), but did not show hydroperoxide stimulation. The authors say that at least for exogenous arachidonic acid 15-HETE is not a true inhibitor, acting by switching substrate use. In cells it also appears to act as a genuine inhibitor, and they report at least two modes of inhibition. Little 5,15-diHETE formed without exogenous arachidonic acid (data not shown).

title: Biological Inactivation of 5-oxo-6,8,11,14-Eicosatetraenoic Acid by Human Platelets
finding: Human platelet and neutrophil mixtures stimulated with A23187 (5 uM) plus PMA (30 nM) made little 5-oxo-ETE but substantial 12-hydroxy metabolites (5-oxo-12-HETE and its 8-trans isomer); platelets alone made no detectable 5-oxo-eicosanoids. Identification was by UV spectra and comparison with chemically synthesised standards, in platelet fractions incubated with 5-HETE. Platelets stimulated with thrombin converted 5-oxo-ETE mainly to the cis and trans 5-oxo-12-HETE isomers, A23187 and thrombin both reducing the 5-ketoreductase metabolites, while resting platelets formed mainly 5-HETE. Some 8-trans isomer is non-enzymatic. The authors suggest platelets may inactivate 5-oxo-ETE in blood.

title: Lipidomics reveals a remarkable diversity of lipids in human plasma
finding: Mass-spectrometric lipidomics of NIST SRM 1950, plasma pooled from 100 fasted adults aged 40 to 50 with an ethnic and sex distribution matching the US population, gave a total of 214 nmol/ml of non-esterified fatty acids across 31 quantified species, of which oleate, palmitate and stearate together accounted for roughly 78 percent, linoleate plus arachidonate for roughly 8 percent, and alpha-linolenate, EPA and DHA together for roughly 1 percent.

title: Completing the uric acid degradation pathway through phylogenetic comparison of whole genomes
finding: Phylogenetic genome comparison found two gene families (COG2351, COG3195) whose gain and loss track urate oxidase. The two recombinant mouse proteins were assayed in vitro (pH 7.6, urate oxidase from Candida utilis): one decomposes 5-hydroxyisourate rapidly, and the other prevents the accumulation of OHCU. S-(+)-allantoin, identified by 13C NMR and circular dichroism, was shown only with all three enzymes present, so the OHCU decarboxylase assignment rests on the proposed scheme. Spontaneous decay gives racemic allantoin over hours (cited from earlier work, ref. 5). The authors call the evolutionary order of gene loss likely but not the only possible scenario.

title: Isolation and sequence determination of a cDNA clone for rat peroxisomal urate oxidase: liver-specific expression in the rat.

Single copy is called suggestive, from an EcoRV digest. In one Northern blot of total RNA from one human liver with the rat probe, no band was seen; the actin check is data not shown. Human genomic DNA has homologous sequences. A note added in proof says a later rat clone differs substantially at both ends.

title: CpG methylation is maintained in human cancer cells lacking DNMT1
finding: In HCT116 cells with DNMT1 disrupted (exons 3 to 5 replaced), methyltransferase activity fell by 66 +/- 4% in DNMT1+/- and 96 +/- 2% in DNMT1-/- cells, but total 5-methylcytosine fell by only 20 +/- 4%. Juxtacentromeric satellite repeats on chromosomes 1, 9, 15 and 16 were demethylated, while alphoid centromeric repeats were not. The 35 CpG sites of the p16INK4a island stayed methylated at about 50%, consistent with monoallelic methylation, and only the mutant allele was expressed, as in parental cells. Other CpG islands are data not shown. The authors do not know whether this holds beyond HCT116 and infer that other methyltransferases suffice.
locator: Results: Fig. 1d, Fig. 2b, Fig. 3b, Fig. 4a to 4c; Discussion

title: DNMT1 and DNMT3b cooperate to silence genes in human cancer cells
finding: In HCT116 cells, deleting DNMT3b reduced global DNA methylation by less than 3%. The DNMT1 plus DNMT3b double knockout lines (DKO 1 and DKO 2 are the representative clones) had DNA methyltransferase activity nearly abolished and genomic methylation reduced by roughly 95% in the main text (greater than 95% in the abstract). One of eight DKO clones, DKO 8, was aberrant, keeping more methylation. Residual methylation might come from another enzyme. The authors say it is not known whether the result applies to other human cell types.
locator: Main text with Fig. 1d and Fig. 2a; Fig. 4

title: An atlas of human metabolism
finding: In the Human1 (Human-GEM) gene essentiality analysis, a gene counts as essential if its deletion impairs any of 57 basic metabolic tasks, biomass production among them, rather than growth alone; the authors state this reduces dependence on the biomass reaction formulation and hypothesise higher sensitivity. Predictions were made on five cell-line-specific models built with tINIT from CRISPR-screened cell lines (GBM, RPE1, HCT116, DLD1, HeLa) and compared with HMR2 and Recon3D.
locator: Results: Prediction of metabolic task-essential genes in human cell lines; Fig. 4A

title: Structural conservation, functional decline: The fate of human OHCU decarboxylase
finding: Recombinant human OHCU decarboxylase (URAD) is a well-folded alpha-helical protein closely similar to the zebrafish enzyme (52% sequence identity, RMSD below 0.8 Angstrom) but less stable, and in functional assays its catalytic activity is markedly lower than that of the zebrafish enzyme; molecular dynamics indicates different ligand binding and altered conformational flexibility in the human protein.

title: Sterol carrier protein X is peroxisomal 3-oxoacyl coenzyme A thiolase with intrinsic sterol carrier and lipid transfer activity.
finding: Purified recombinant rat SCPx-547 cleaved 3-oxoacyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA and the chain-shortened acyl-CoA, with the highest activity for 3-oxooctanoyl-CoA. It stimulated microsomal conversion of 7-dehydrocholesterol to cholesterol less than SCP2, transferred phosphatidylcholine at 34% of the molar activity of SCP2 and 7-dehydrocholesterol at 53%. SCPx epitopes were found mainly in peroxisomes, with some in the cytosol. The thiolase-like domain alone (SCPx-383) had no detectable activity, but the authors say this does not settle that it is insufficient. Homology to other thiolases is low (about 25%). The abstract says the data suggest a peroxisomal thiolase; the conclusion states it.
locator: Results and Discussion: Fig. 6 (thiolase), Fig. 7 and Table II (transfer), Figs. 3-5 and Table I (localization)

title: Coenzyme Q headgroup intermediates can ameliorate a mitochondrial encephalopathy
finding: Hpdl-/- mice (untreated pups die by P15) incorporated orally given 13C6-4-hydroxymandelate or 13C6-4-hydroxybenzoate into brain CoQ9 and CoQ10, and 10 mg/kg/day from P3-P5 to P30 let 90-100% reach adulthood, whereas CoQ9 or CoQ10 supplementation did not; 4-HB also stabilised symptoms in one patient with biallelic HPDL variants.

title: DNMT3L Stimulates the DNA Methylation Activity of Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b through a Direct Interaction
finding: Recombinant mouse Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b (from Sf9 cells) were stimulated dose-dependently by GST-tagged human DNMT3L from E. coli: about 1.4 to 1.5-fold for Dnmt3a and more than 2-fold for Dnmt3b (1.5 to 3-fold in the abstract), with maximum at a 10 to 30-fold molar excess; Dnmt1 was not stimulated. Stimulation occurred with all sequences tested, including imprinted differentially methylated regions. DNMT3L bound Dnmt3a and Dnmt3b (Kd roughly 1e-7 M) but not a 5S rDNA fragment (the only DNA tested). The C-terminal half carried the effect. The authors say it may not be DNA targeting but may be a direct effect on catalysis, and that the mechanism is not resolved.
locator: Results: first section, Fig. 1B-D; Fig. 2; Figs. 3-5; Fig. 6

title: The acyl- and alkyl-glycerone phosphate reductase DHRS7 is involved in the production of distinct plasmalogen species from DHRS7B
finding: In human knockout and double-knockout cells, DHRS7 and DHRS7B both contribute to ethanolamine plasmalogen synthesis but to different species: DHRS7 contributes most to C18:1, then C16:0 and C22:4, while DHRS7B contributes to all species measured; DHRS7 localises to the endoplasmic reticulum and DHRS7B to peroxisomes, and in vitro DHRS7 shows both alkyl- and acyl-glycerone phosphate reductase activity, as DHRS7B does.

title: Protection and reactivation of human methylmalonyl-CoA mutase by MMAA protein
finding: With purified recombinant human proteins, MMAA added at the start of the reaction prevented loss of methylmalonyl-CoA mutase activity over long incubation times (activity increasing to 76%, relative to the reference given in the paper), with no effect over short intervals; protection did not need GTP hydrolysis (GMPPNP also worked) and the authors give interference with inactivation as a probable reason. MMAA added after 60 min raised activity with GTP, but not alone or with GMPPNP; exchange of the damaged cofactor is the authors' interpretation. Human mutase did not stimulate the GTPase activity of MMAA. A yeast two-hybrid test indicated interaction, with faint colour in some controls. The MMAA preparation was partly degraded.
locator: Results: 3.3 MCM activity and the effect of MMAA, Fig. 3; 3.4, Fig. 4; Discussion

title: Molecular and Functional Identification of Sodium Ion-dependent, High Affinity Human Carnitine Transporter OCTN2
finding: Human OCTN2 expressed in HEK293 cells gave a large uptake of L-carnitine. Replacing sodium almost abolished uptake (lithium kept a weak activity), but OCTN2 raised uptake with and without sodium, and HEK293 cells have a weak sodium-dependent carnitine uptake of their own. Km 4.34 +/- 0.602 (the extracted text prints the unit as mM, the micro sign being lost throughout; check the PDF). One site on an Eadie-Hofstee plot. TEA and guanidine were hardly transported. Northern blots showed strong adult expression in kidney, skeletal muscle, placenta, heart, prostate and thyroid. OCTN1 gave slight carnitine uptake. The symbol SLC22A5 does not appear in the paper.
locator: Results: Functional Analysis of OCTN2 Expressed in HEK293 Cells, Fig. 3, Fig. 4; Amino Acid Sequence and Tissue Distribution, Fig. 2

title: Human Metastasis Regulator Protein H-Prune is a Short-Chain Exopolyphosphatase
finding: Recombinant His-tagged human h-prune hydrolysed short-chain polyphosphates efficiently (kcat 3 to 40 per s), including tri- and tetrapolyphosphate, but not pyrophosphate, ATP, GTP or cAMP. Polyphosphates of 25 or more residues reacted much more slowly. It needs Mg2+, Co2+ or Mn2+; Co2+ is better for kcat but not kcat/Km. Activity was suppressed by nm23-H1, long-chain polyphosphates and pyrophosphate, which the authors call potential physiological regulators. Mutating seven residues matching the yeast exopolyphosphatase active site severely lowered activity, while one variant had enhanced activity. No endopolyphosphatase activity was detected. In vitro only.
locator: Results: Exopolyphosphatase Activity of H-Prune, Table 1; Inhibitors, Table 3; Active Site Mutations, Table 2

title: Carnitine biosynthesis in mammals
finding: Review of mammalian carnitine biosynthesis stating that the pathway starts from trimethyllysine set free when methylated proteins are hydrolysed in lysosomes, that the aldolase cleaving 3-hydroxy-trimethyllysine may be serine hydroxymethyltransferase (cytosolic isoform the more likely candidate, on the basis of earlier work showing rabbit liver SHMT cleaves HTML, with the identity left unsettled), and that of the tissues assayed only kidney, liver and brain carry the full enzyme set because butyrobetaine dioxygenase is confined to them, so other tissues export butyrobetaine and take up carnitine from the circulation.
locator: Introduction and Figure 2B; HTMLA section; Tissue distribution of carnitine-biosynthetic enzymes and Figure 4

title: Substrate specificity of human carnitine acetyltransferase: Implications for fatty acid and branched-chain amino acid metabolism
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: Recombinant human carnitine acetyltransferase (mitochondrial form shown, peroxisomal form reported identical) converted short- and medium-chain acyl-CoAs (C2 to C10) to acylcarnitines, quantified by ESI-MS/MS. The Results report some activity with C12 and C14 but not C16, while the Discussion describes hardly any activity with C12 and C14 and none detectable with C16; the two statements conflict. Trans-2-enoyl-CoAs were poor substrates, and branched-chain acyl-CoAs had much lower affinity than straight-chain ones. It was active with some but not all branched-chain amino acid oxidation intermediates tested, and not with malonyl-, methylmalonyl-, succinyl- or glutaryl-CoA. 3-Hydroxyisovaleryl-CoA and 3-methylglutaconyl-CoA were not available to test. In vitro, recombinant enzyme only.
locator: Results 3.1 with Fig. 1, Fig. 2 and Table 1; Discussion

title: A genome-wide atlas of co-essential modules assigns function to uncharacterized genes
finding: A co-essentiality atlas across CRISPR screens placed TMEM189 in an ether lipid synthesis module; HeLa-Cas9 cells with TMEM189-targeting sgRNAs had much lower levels of 37 plasmenylethanolamine (plasmalogen) species and higher levels of 30 plasmanylethanolamine precursor species, identifying TMEM189 as plasmanylethanolamine desaturase.
locator: Results: TMEM189 encodes the enzyme PEDS required for plasmalogen synthesis; Fig. 4c-e

title: Sterol Carrier Protein X (SCPx) Is a Peroxisomal Branched-Chain β-Ketothiolase Specifically Reacting with 3-Oxo-pristanoyl-CoA: A New, Unique Role for SCPx in Branched-Chain Fatty Acid Metabolism in Peroxisomes
finding: Rat liver peroxisomal 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase (the conventional enzyme) showed virtually no activity with 3-oxopristanoyl-CoA (Fig. 1). Recombinant rat SCPx (547 residues, made in E. coli) cleaved 3-oxopristanoyl-CoA with its highest activity, and also reacted with 3-oxopalmitoyl-CoA, so it is not specific for the branched substrate. The authors conclude that SCPx has a central role in branched-chain fatty acid beta-oxidation in peroxisomes and suggest it is essential for pristanic acid; data on cholestanoic acid esters are preliminary. Rat protein.
locator: Results: Fig. 1 and Fig. 2; Table 1; Abstract

title: Genetic dissection of polyunsaturated fatty acid synthesis in Caenorhabditis elegans
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: C. elegans mutants isolated by direct fatty acid analysis: fat-1 (n3 desaturase), fat-2 (delta-12), fat-3 (delta-6), fat-4 (delta-5) and elo-1 (C18 to C20 elongation). With them every step from 18:1n9 to 20:5n3 is represented, except the delta-9 desaturases fat-5, fat-6 and fat-7, which the screen did not mutate; elo-1 mutants keep C20 PUFAs, so another elongase is likely. Compositions show the substrate preferences. fat-1 and fat-4 mutants are indistinguishable from wild type under laboratory conditions (20 C, E. coli diet), and C20 PUFAs are about 40% in fat-1, fat-4 and wild type. fat-2 and fat-3 mutants grow slowly, move sluggishly and have a reduced brood size; fat-2 also has abnormal body shape and cuticle defects. No neurological assay is reported; the defects are in growth and movement.
locator: Results: fat-1, fat-2, fat-3, fat-4 and elo-1 sections; Fig. 3, Table 1, Fig. 4

title: The TMEM189 gene encodes plasmanylethanolamine desaturase which introduces the characteristic vinyl ether double bond into plasmalogens
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Mice homozygous for an inactivating Tmem189 knockout-first allele had kidney plasmanylethanolamine desaturase activity below the detection limit of 0.2 pmol per mg per min, had almost completely lost plasmalogens in kidney and in 12 other tissues, and had reduced body weight in both sexes (n = 3 per group); the mice reached adult phenotyping age.
locator: Results: Tmem189-Deficient Mice Lack Both PEDS Activity and Plasmalogens; Fig. 4

title: Synthesis, structural identification and biological activity of 11,12-dihydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids formed in human platelets
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Lipids and Lipid Metabolism
finding: Aspirin-treated human platelets incubated with arachidonic acid made 11,12-dihydroxyeicosatetraenoic acids. Comparison with synthetic standards by HPLC and GC retention and GC-MS fragmentation identified the major isomer as 11(R),12(S)-dihydroxy-5Z,7E,9E,14Z-eicosatetraenoic acid. A second major isomer (compound III) was identified only tentatively as the 5E,7E,9E,14Z form, its hydroxyl geometry unknown and no standard cochromatographed with it. The authors propose formation by a leukotriene-like epoxide route, probably through 12-lipoxygenase, which they say is not established. The abstract says the major compound lacks biological activity in the test systems used. The scan is partly unreadable.

title: cDNA cloning, characterization, and tissue-specific expression of human xanthine dehydrogenase/xanthine oxidase.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: cDNAs for human xanthine dehydrogenase were isolated from a liver library and the complete sequence was determined: one open reading frame of 1336 residues, Mr 147,782. The abstract describes a potential 2Fe/2S binding site and a putative molybdopterin cofactor binding domain. A model for conversion to xanthine oxidase by cysteine oxidation or limited proteolysis is a hypothesis. RNA blots show a single 5100-base RNA in liver, with strong tissue dependence, and a smaller 4500-base RNA of uncertain origin in heart, brain and kidney. The paper mentions uric acid once, as the product of the hydroxylation of hypoxanthine and xanthine by XD (introduction, citing refs 4 and 5). It does not study urate oxidation or allantoin formation.
locator: Results: Human XD Gene Organization and Nucleotide Sequence; Fig. 2. Results: Expression of Human XD; Fig. 4

title: Two independent mutational events in the loss of urate oxidase during hominoid evolution
finding: Human and chimpanzee urate oxidase genes carry nonsense mutations at codons 33 and 187 and an aberrant splice acceptor in exon 3. Orangutan carries only the codon 33 nonsense mutation. Gibbon has none of the three; instead a 13-bp deletion disrupts the reading frame. The chimpanzee, orangutan and gibbon were examined only at the mutation sites, with DNA from cell lines. The authors suggest two independent events after the gibbon lineage diverged, while saying a single ancestral mutation is not completely excluded and other gibbon mutations were not explored. The codon 187 and splice mutations in human and chimpanzee are placed after the gene was inactivated. Tree and dates come from earlier work.
locator: Abstract; Results: Occurrence of the Three Mutations in Other Hominoids; A 13-bp Deletion in the Gibbon Gene; Table 1; Fig. 6

title: Hyperuricemia and urate nephropathy in urate oxidase-deficient mice.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: The mouse urate oxidase gene was disrupted by a neomycin cassette in exon 3 in embryonic stem cells. Homozygous mutants had serum uric acid of 11.0 +/- 1.7 mg per 100 ml, about 10 times that of wild-type and heterozygous mice, and progressive kidney destruction with lesions confined to the kidneys. Of 150 offspring of homozygous matings (hybrid C57BL/6J x 129Sv background) 97 (65%) died within 4 weeks. The few survivors were viable and fertile. Lethality may depend on the genetic background: only 3 homozygous mutants among 99 offspring of heterozygous matings on the 129Sv background. Allopurinol treatment improved survival. The authors conclude that urate oxidase is essential in the mouse and possibly in other mammals that keep the enzyme.
locator: Results: Targeted Disruption of Urate Oxidase Gene; Development of Hyperuricemia and Urate Nephropathy; Urate Oxidase Gene Targeting Causes Lethality; Table 1; Fig. 4-6

title: Resveratrol and para-coumarate serve as ring precursors for coenzyme Q biosynthesis
finding: 13C6-resveratrol (70 uM, 24 h) gave labelled CoQ10 in three human cell lines and labelled CoQ9 in mouse 3T3 fibroblasts, at about 10% of total CoQ10 in the mammalian cells, and labelled CoQ in wild-type yeast at under 1%, and as trace amounts in wild-type E. coli, with more in a ubiC mutant. 13C6-coumarate gave labelled CoQ in yeast, E. coli and human U251 cells; no mouse cells were tested with it. 13C6-pABA gave none in E. coli (including a ubiC mutant) or in human U251 cells, the only mammalian line tested with pABA. Isotope tracing only; the conversion pathway and the enzymes are not identified.

title: Human methionine synthase reductase is a molecular chaperone for human methionine synthase
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Recombinant human methionine synthase and its reductase were purified from baculovirus-infected insect cells. The reductase maintained activity of purified holoenzyme at a 1:1 ratio with Kact 71 nM (assay with DTT present). In crude Sf21 extract it protected the apoenzyme against loss and raised holoenzyme formation, but it did not rescue denatured apoenzyme. With NADPH it reduced free aquacobalamin to cob(II)alamin at 37 C but not at 22 C. It raised holoenzyme formation from apoenzyme plus aquacobalamin also without NADPH, so protection and reduction are not separated; the authors call the reduction explanation probable and propose a chaperone plus aquacobalamin reductase role. It did not activate E. coli methionine synthase.
locator: Results: Reductive Activation of hMS by hMSR; Fig. 2. Results: MS Apoenzyme Protection by MSR; Fig. 4. Results: Reduction of Free aqCbl by Human MSR; Fig. 5, Table 3

title: ELOVL4 protein preferentially elongates 20:5n3 to very long chain PUFAs over 20:4n6 and 22:6n3
finding: In rat PC12 cells transduced with mouse Elovl4, with non-transduced and GFP-transduced cells as controls, only the ELOVL4-expressing cells made C28 to C38 very long chain PUFA, whereas controls, which carry endogenous Elovl1, Elovl2, Elovl4 message and abundant Elovl5 but no detectable ELOVL4 protein, elongated supplemented 20:5n-3, 22:6n-3 and 20:4n-6 to C22 to C26 products and formed 24:5n-3 as well, with 20:5n-3, 22:5n-3 and 24:5n-3 levels not differing significantly between ELOVL4 and control cells after 20:5n-3 supplementation; the authors ascribe this ELOVL4-independent elongation to endogenous ELOVL5 or ELOVL2.
locator: Results: Expression of ELOVL4 and elongation of supplemented FAs; Figs. 2A, 3A, 4A; Discussion

title: BBOX1 Deficiency Exacerbates Liver Fibrosis Through Carnitine Biosynthesis Disruption Rescued by Carnitine Supplementation
finding: In global Bbox1 knockout mice (males, 8 to 10 weeks) liver free carnitine was about one-tenth of wild type (0.21 vs 2.16 ug/g), and the knockouts had metabolic abnormalities without injury. Under thioacetamide the knockouts developed more severe fibrosis, and the text says dietary L-carnitine completely rescued this. The authors link the effect to TRPC6-Ca2+/CAMK2B signalling, but they did not block TRPC6 in vivo, and a global knockout cannot say which cell type is responsible.
