Public transcriptomes show lower BBOX1 mRNA in human cirrhosis and alcoholic hepatitis. One toxin model (thioacetamide).
locator: Results 3.1 with Fig. 1; 3.2 with Fig. 2C; 3.4 with Fig. 4; 3.5 with Fig. 5; Discussion

title: Identification of the peroxisomal β-oxidation enzymes involved in the degradation of leukotrienes
finding: Leukotriene beta-oxidation in peroxisomes needs D-bifunctional protein (HSD17B4); ALDP (ABCD1) and peroxisomal 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase (ACAA1) are not involved.

title: High-Resolution CRISPR Screens Reveal Fitness Genes and Genotype-Specific Cancer Liabilities
finding: CRISPR fitness screens in five human cell lines (DLD1, GBM, HCT116, HeLa, RPE1); the reference for Human-GEM's gene-essentiality test.

title: The Biosynthesis of Uroporphyrinogen III: Mechanism of Action of Porphobilinogen Deaminase
finding: Symposium review of how porphobilinogen deaminase builds the tetrapyrrole hydroxymethylbilane; it states that without the cosynthase (uroporphyrinogen III synthase) this product cyclises on its own to uroporphyrinogen I. The structural and mutagenesis parts concern the E. coli deaminase, and the spontaneous-cyclisation statement is a summary, not a new measurement.

title: Activation of human erythrocyte 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate phosphatase at physiological concentrations of substrate
finding: Enzyme-kinetic study of the purified human erythrocyte enzyme: in these cells the reactions of the 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate shunt are catalysed mainly by a single protein with synthase and phosphatase activity, and its phosphatase is activated by phosphate and sulfite, also at 5 mM 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate. In vitro with purified enzyme; the abstract does not name the gene.

title: NDUFA4 Is a Subunit of Complex IV of the Mammalian Electron Transport Chain
finding: Proteomic, genetic, evolutionary and biochemical analyses indicate that NDUFA4, formerly assigned to complex I, belongs to cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV): deleting NDUFA4 left complex I intact and affected complex IV function and assembly. The authors propose renaming the gene and treating it as a candidate for complex IV rather than complex I deficiency.

title: Expanding coincident signaling by PTEN through its inositol 1,3,4,5,6-pentakisphosphate 3-phosphatase activity
finding: PTEN purified after expression in bacteria or HEK cells removed the 3-phosphate of inositol 1,3,4,5,6-pentakisphosphate (Km 7.1 uM versus 26 uM for PtdIns(3,4,5)P3), and transient PTEN expression in HEK cells lowered the cellular level of this inositol phosphate. Contradicted in U87-MG cells by Orchiston 2004 (10.1074/jbc.m310933200), where wild-type PTEN did not change inositol phosphate levels.

title: The mechanism of formation of o-bromophenol from bromobenzene.
finding: In liver microsomes from 3-methylcholanthrene-treated rats, a bromobenzene 2,3-dihydrodiol was isolated and the deuterium label of o-bromophenol was largely retained, with no isotope effect; this indicates formation via bromobenzene-2,3-oxide rather than direct oxygen insertion. The authors state the result does not exclude oxygen addition followed by an NIH shift, and the abstract does not address spontaneous versus enzymatic isomerisation of the oxide.

title: Isolation and Sequencing of Salsolinol Synthase, an Enzyme Catalyzing Salsolinol Biosynthesis
finding: A 77-residue, 8.6 kDa ubiquitin-like protein was purified from rat brain and reported as salsolinol synthase; overexpression in eukaryotic cells raised salsolinol production over control. It makes salsolinol from dopamine and acetaldehyde in this system; no human gene is given.

title: 9-O-Acetylation of sialic acids is catalysed by CASD1 via a covalent acetyl-enzyme intermediate
finding: CRISPR/Cas knockout of CASD1 in human cells abolished sialic acid 9-O-acetylation, and the purified luminal domain moved acetyl groups from acetyl-CoA to CMP-activated sialic acid through a covalent acetyl-enzyme intermediate. The substrate shown is CMP-sialic acid, not a ganglioside.

title: Genetic evidence that the human CYP2R1 enzyme is a key vitamin D 25-hydroxylase
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: A patient with low circulating 25-hydroxyvitamin D and vitamin D deficiency was homozygous for a CYP2R1 missense change (Leu99Pro) that removed vitamin D 25-hydroxylase activity. One patient; the paper identifies CYP2R1 as a relevant hepatic 25-hydroxylase.

title: Alpha-tocopheryl hydroquinone is an efficient multifunctional inhibitor of radical-initiated oxidation of low density lipoprotein lipids
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: In isolated human LDL, alpha-tocopheryl hydroquinone instantly reduced the lipoprotein's ubiquinone-10 to ubiquinol-10 and also scavenged radicals, acting as an antioxidant. In vitro on lipoprotein; the abstract does not mention an enzyme, so the reduction is non-enzymatic.

title: Stereoselective Formation and Metabolism of 4-Hydroxy-Retinoic Acid Enantiomers by Cytochrome P450 Enzymes
finding: Recombinant CYP26A1 formed mainly (4S)-4-hydroxy-retinoic acid, CYP3A4 formed both enantiomers equally, CYP3A5 favoured (4R), and CYP3A7 and CYP2C8 favoured (4S). CYP26A1 cleared (4S) about three times faster than (4R) and made 4-oxo-retinoic acid only from (4R); CYP26B1 and CYP26C1 are not tested in the abstract.

title: Evidence against Functionally Significant Aquaporin Expression in Mitochondria
finding: Mitochondrial membranes from rat brain, liver and kidney, and from wild-type and AQP-null mice, had similar osmotic water and glycerol permeabilities, and AQP8 was not detected by immunoblot in mouse liver mitochondria. The authors conclude aquaporins are not functionally significant there; H2O2 permeability was not measured.

title: Identities and Differences in the Metabolism of Tocotrienols and Tocopherols in HepG2 Cells
finding: In HepG2 cells alpha- and gamma-tocotrienol were degraded by omega- then beta-oxidation of the side chain to carboxychromanols; the intermediate with the original side-chain double bond (CMBHC) was not detected, so auxiliary enzymes as for unsaturated fatty acids are implied. One cell line; no genes tested.

title: Mutations in SRD5B1 (AKR1D1), the gene encoding delta(4)-3-oxosteroid 5beta-reductase, in hepatitis and liver failure in infancy
finding: Three infants with neonatal cholestatic liver disease whose main urinary and plasma bile acids were 3-oxo-delta4 species carried homozygous AKR1D1 (SRD5B1) mutations (two missense, one frameshift). Three patients; it describes the accumulating bile acids and not the order of steps in side-chain shortening.

title: Plasma Metanephrines Are Markers of Pheochromocytoma Produced by Catechol-O-Methyltransferase Within Tumors
journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
finding: In pheochromocytoma patients, free metanephrines in tumour tissue exceeded plasma levels more than 10,000-fold, and over 93 percent of circulating metanephrines were calculated to come from catecholamine metabolism inside the tumour (COMT, mainly membrane-bound) before release. It does not test whether an ATP-driven export of normetanephrine exists.

title: Human carnitine biosynthesis proceeds via (2S,3S)-3-hydroxy-Nε-trimethyllysine
finding: Enzymatic and asymmetric chemical synthesis experiments define the product of trimethyllysine hydroxylase (TMLH, the first step of mammalian carnitine biosynthesis) as the (2S,3S) stereoisomer of 3-hydroxy-N-epsilon-trimethyllysine; the abstract does not report kinetics or a cell-based test.

title: Carnitine biosynthesis in mammals
organism: mammals (emphasis on Homo sapiens and Rattus norvegicus)
finding: Review of the enzymes, genes and regulation of mammalian carnitine biosynthesis. It leaves the submitochondrial site of trimethyllysine dioxygenase open and places most hydroxytrimethyllysine aldolase activity in the soluble fraction of human tissue, which makes a cytosolic isoenzyme more likely. This DOI string is an alternative form of the DOI 10.1042/bj3610417 of the same review.
locator: Review sections on trimethyllysine dioxygenase and hydroxytrimethyllysine aldolase (subcellular location)

title: Identification and Characterization of a Membrane Protein (y+L Amino Acid Transporter-1) That Associates with 4F2hc to Encode the Amino Acid Transport Activity y+L
finding: A cloned human cDNA (y+LAT-1) co-expressed with the 4F2 heavy chain (4F2hc) in Xenopus oocytes induced y+L amino acid transport and formed a disulfide-linked heterodimer with 4F2hc; mutating 4F2hc Cys109 abolished the heterodimer and sharply reduced transport. The mRNA is mainly in kidney, the gene maps to the lysinuric protein intolerance locus, and the authors propose it as a candidate gene; the abstract does not give per-substrate exchange specificity for the individual amino acid antiports.

title: The Molecular Architecture of Human N-Acetylgalactosamine Kinase
finding: Crystal structures of human GalNAc kinase (GALK2) with MnAMPPNP and GalNAc or with MgATP and GalNAc (bound products) place it in the GHMP kinase superfamily and define the determinants of GalNAc specificity; the abstract reports GalNAc as the substrate studied and gives no activity measurements.

title: Vesicular GABA transporter (VGAT) transports β-alanine
finding: Proteoliposomes with purified VGAT took up beta-alanine driven by membrane potential and requiring chloride, and VGAT also promoted chloride uptake with beta-alanine; the Glu213Ala mutant that disrupts GABA and glycine transport also abolished beta-alanine uptake. In vitro reconstituted system only; the organism of the VGAT used is not stated in the abstract (organism assumed mouse/rodent, unverified).

title: Expression and Characterization of CYP4V2 as a Fatty Acid ω-Hydroxylase
finding: Recombinant CYP4V2 was a selective omega-hydroxylase of saturated medium-chain fatty acids, most efficient with myristic acid, and was inhibited at nanomolar concentration by HET0016. In vitro with expressed enzyme; the link to Bietti's crystalline dystrophy is proposed by the authors. The abstract does not name CYP4A11 or CYP4A22 (also in the GPR of the reactions).

title: The Reduction of α-Tocopherolquinone by Human NAD(P)H:Quinone Oxidoreductase: The Role of α-Tocopherolhydroquinone as a Cellular Antioxidant
finding: Purified human NQO1 reduced alpha-tocopherolquinone to the hydroquinone (Km 370 uM, kcat 5.6e3 per min) and did so more efficiently than coenzyme Q10; in CHO cells expressing human NQO1 the hydroquinone formed correlated with NQO1 activity and protected against lipid peroxidation. Purified enzyme plus a hamster cell model; the abstract does not mention CBR1 (also in the GPR).

title: Cholestenoic acids regulate motor neuron survival via liver X receptors
finding: Cholestenoic acids from the bile acid pathway were profiled in mammalian CSF and shown to act on liver X receptors in motor neurons (zebrafish, mouse in vitro and in vivo); patients with CYP7B1 deficiency (SPG5) had excess 3beta-hydroxycholest-5-en-26-oic acid and those with CYP27A1 deficiency (CTX) had low 3beta,7alpha-dihydroxycholest-5-en-26-oic acid in CSF and plasma. The abstract does not describe the individual enzyme steps that MAR01794 and MAR01796 represent, so the support for those reactions is indirect, from the patient metabolite profiles.

title: Molecular Genetics of 3β-Hydroxy-Δ5-C27-Steroid Oxidoreductase Deficiency in 16 Patients with Loss of Bile Acid Synthesis and Liver Disease
journal: The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism
finding: Twelve different HSD3B7 mutations were found in 15 further patients (13 kindreds) with loss of bile acid synthesis and cholestatic liver disease; ten mutations tested caused complete loss of enzyme activity, so C27 3beta-HSD in the endoplasmic reticulum is needed for bile acid synthesis. The abstract does not name the 7alpha-hydroxycholesterol substrate of MAR01584 specifically.

title: Mitochondrial β-Oxidation of 2-Methyl Fatty Acids in Rat Liver
finding: Coupled rat liver mitochondria and purified enzymes: the trifunctional beta-oxidation complex hydrates, dehydrogenates and cleaves medium- and long-chain 2-methyl-branched substrates, whereas the matrix L-3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase and 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase are inactive with them. Rat only; no vitamin E carboxychromanol intermediate was tested, so the use for the tocotrienol rounds is an inference.

title: Adenosine phosphorylase activity as distinct from inosine-guanosine phosphorylase activity in sarcoma 180 cells and rat liver
finding: Argues that an adenosine-phosphorylating activity in sarcoma 180 cells and rat liver is distinct from inosine-guanosine (purine nucleoside) phosphorylase. Nicotinate riboside is not among the substrates, so the paper does not support nicotinate riboside phosphorolysis by PNP (cited as a reference of MAR04662).

title: Model-based assessment of mammalian cell metabolic functionalities using omics data
finding: Presents CellFie: curated and standardized lists of metabolic tasks of mammalian cells, with gene sets per task derived from genome-scale models and a scoring of omics data on them, applied to transcriptomes from single cells to tissues. Source of the CellFie task numbering and definitions (for example tasks 7, 21, 22, 64, 82, 90, 107, 130, 148, 161, 169, 178, 184, 187) that the drafts correct; the task list itself was not checked beyond the abstract.

title: Functional identification of a vesicular acetylcholine transporter and its expression from a “cholinergic” gene locus.
finding: Rat VAChT expressed in CV-1 cells gave proton-dependent, vesamicol-sensitive acetylcholine accumulation. Stoichiometry was not measured; rat protein only.

title: Cutaneous expression of cytochrome P450 CYP2S1: individuality in regulation by therapeutic agents for psoriasis and other skin diseases
finding: RT-PCR in skin of 27 healthy volunteers and 29 psoriasis patients: CYP2S1 is expressed in skin with large individual variation and is induced by UV, PUVA, coal tar and all-trans retinoic acid. The abstract reports regulation of expression, not metabolism of retinoic acid by the enzyme; the claim that CYP2S1 metabolises retinoate is not stated in the abstract and the full text was not read.

title: Stoichiometry of hydrogen ion-linked dopamine transport in chromaffin granule ghosts
finding: Bovine chromaffin granule ghosts take up dopamine with a stoichiometry of two H+ per dopamine. Other amines and acetylcholine are covered only by analogy; not human.

title: The metabolites NADP+ and NADPH are the targets of the circadian protein Nocturnin (Curled)
finding: NOCT converts NADP+ to NAD+ and NADPH to NADH in vitro (Fig. 1c, 2a). Overexpressed full-length tagged NOCT in A549 cells localised to mitochondria; only a construct lacking the mitochondrial targeting sequence was cytosolic (Fig. 3c-d), so the paper gives no evidence for native cytosolic NOCT. The authors mention only as a possibility that NOCT may also act outside mitochondria.
locator: Results: NOCT activity, mitochondrial localisation; Fig. 1c, 2a, 3c-d

title: Dephosphorylation of 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate by MIPP expands the regulatory capacity of the Rapoport–Luebering glycolytic shunt
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Dictyostelium, bird and mammalian MIPP1 (MINPP1) hydrolyses 2,3-bisphosphoglycerate by removing the 3-phosphate, a route that bypasses 3-phosphoglycerate, unlike BPGM, which removes the 2-phosphate. Erythrocyte MIPP1 activity at 37 C was 0.6 mmol per litre of cells per hour, similar to published BPGM phosphatase estimates. Abstract only; the 2-phosphatase activity of BPGM is background in this paper.

title: Identification of the GalNAc Kinase Amino Acid Sequence
finding: Identifies the GalNAc kinase sequence (pig enzyme, human GALK2 cDNA). The enzyme also phosphorylates galactose, with a Km of about 4 mM for the pig enzyme, and the human cDNA rescued a gal1 yeast mutant, so GALK2 has some galactokinase activity besides being the GalNAc kinase.

title: Generation, Release, and Uptake of the NAD Precursor Nicotinic Acid Riboside by Human Cells
finding: Purified recombinant human cytosolic 5'-nucleotidases CN-II (NT5C2) and CN-III (NT5C3A), but not CN-IA (NT5C1A), dephosphorylate NMN and NAMN in vitro, at millimolar substrate concentrations. Overexpression of CN-II and CN-III in HEK293 and HepG2 cells formed and released nicotinic acid riboside; untransfected HeLa cells release NAR and NR.

title: Nicotinamide Riboside and Nicotinic Acid Riboside Salvage in Fungi and Mammals
finding: Purified bovine purine nucleoside phosphorylase was about 120 times more active on nicotinic acid riboside than yeast Pnp1 (Table 1, p. 163). Human PNP was not tested on this substrate, so the paper supports the activity for bovine PNP only.

title: Kinetic analysis of human CYP24A1 metabolism of vitamin D via the C24-oxidation pathway
finding: Partially purified human CYP24A1 in a phospholipid-vesicle system metabolised 1,25(OH)2D3 and C24-pathway intermediates (Km 0.34 to 15 mmol per mol phospholipid, kcat up to 34 per min). Side-chain cleavage of 24-oxo-1,23,25(OH)3D3 was the most efficient step and gave 1-hydroxy-23-oxo-tetranor-D3, not 1,23-dihydroxy-tetranor-D3, as primary product; the abstract does not state the fate of the C4 product or calcitroic acid formation.

title: Recent Advances in Carrier-Mediated Intestinal Absorption of Water-Soluble Vitamins
finding: Review of carrier-mediated intestinal absorption of water-soluble vitamins (ascorbate, biotin, folate, riboflavin, thiamin, pyridoxine), covering driving forces, molecular identity and regulation of the transporters. Cited as a reference of MAR06512 (FAD exchange); the abstract does not mention FAD transport and the four genes of that reaction are not transporters.

title: Cloning of Human 25-Hydroxyvitamin D-1α-Hydroxylase and Mutations Causing Vitamin D-Dependent Rickets Type 1
finding: cDNA of 25-hydroxyvitamin D 1-alpha-hydroxylase (P450c1alpha) cloned from human keratinocytes; transfected mammalian cells made 1,25(OH)2D3 (HPLC and GC-MS), and keratinocytes of a patient with vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1 lacked the activity and carried frameshift mutations. Vitamin D3 to calcitriol (CellFie task 261).

title: Molecular Cloning of Human Mitochondrial Glycerophosphate Dehydrogenase Gene: Genomic Structure, Chromosomal Localization, and Existence of a Pseudogene
finding: Cloned the cDNA of human mitochondrial glycerophosphate dehydrogenase from an insulinoma library, mapped the gene to chromosome 2q23, worked out its 15-exon structure and found a pseudogene on 19q13.4. It is a gene-structure paper with no enzyme assay or reaction data, so it does not describe the reaction chemistry of MAR00449.

title: The reaction of β-mercaptop0ruvate with lactic dehydrogenase of heart muscle
finding: Title only is available (Europe PMC has no abstract); it reports a reaction of 3-mercaptopyruvate with lactate dehydrogenase from heart muscle. Species and isoenzyme are not stated in what was read; the draft cites it for LDHA/LDHB-type enzymes only, so it does not show the reaction for LDHC or LDHAL6A.

title: In vitro biosynthesis of 3-mercaptolactate by lactate dehydrogenases
organism: Rattus norvegicus;Gloeobacter violaceus;Escherichia coli;Corynebacterium glutamicum;Bacillus cereus
finding: Purified recombinant bacterial lactate dehydrogenases were tested for reduction of 3-mercaptopyruvate to 3-mercaptolactate, with rat liver LDH as comparator: the Gloeobacter enzyme reached 63.6 U/mg (about twice the rat enzyme) and the E. coli, C. glutamicum and B. cereus enzymes had little or no activity. The rat liver LDH is described as active on 3-mercaptopyruvate; no human LDH was tested.

title: Carnitine biosynthesis. beta-Hydroxylation of trimethyllysine by an alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent mitochondrial dioxygenase.
finding: Rat liver mitochondria hydroxylated trimethyllysine to 3-hydroxy-trimethyllysine with alpha-ketoglutarate, Fe2+ and ascorbate, while microsomal and soluble fractions had no activity; the product was cleaved by serine hydroxymethyltransferase to gamma-butyrobetaine aldehyde and glycine. The preliminary digitonin data in the paper point to the outer rather than the inner mitochondrial membrane, so the matrix site rests on UniProt, not on this paper; rat only.

title: Dopamine-Derived Salsolinol Derivatives as Endogenous Monoamine Oxidase Inhibitors: Occurrence, Metabolism and Function in Human Brains
finding: Review which states that the (R) enantiomers of salsolinol derivatives predominate in human brain and are made by an enzyme, (R)-salsolinol synthase, not by the non-enzymatic Pictet-Spengler condensation. The review gives no gene for the synthase and does not itself report the primary assay.

title: Catalytic Function of Nongastric H,K-ATPase Expressed in Sf-21 Insect Cells
finding: Human ATP12A (nongastric H,K-ATPase alpha subunit) co-expressed with the gastric beta subunit (ATP4B) in Sf-21 insect cell membranes gave an active K+-stimulated ATPase (Km for K+ about 116 uM) that is partly inhibited by ouabain; neither protein alone gave activity. Heterologous expression in insect cells only.

title: One substrate many enzymes virtual screening uncovers missing genes of carnitine biosynthesis in human and mouse
finding: Docking of a substrate to AlphaFold models of vitamin B6 enzymes, followed by experimental testing, showed that SHMT1 and SHMT2 catalyse the hydroxytrimethyllysine aldolase step of carnitine biosynthesis; a mouse threonine aldolase (Tha1) that humans lack does it more efficiently. The authors suggest that SHMT activity partly makes up for this gene loss in humans.

title: A catechol-O-methyltransferase that is essential for auditory function in mice and humans
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Positional cloning in mice identified a previously unannotated catechol-O-methyltransferase (COMT2) whose missense mutation causes deafness and vestibular defects and lowers enzyme activity; a nonsense mutation in the human ortholog causes nonsyndromic deafness. The paper establishes the gene and its methyltransferase function; it says nothing about Ensembl identifiers in Human-GEM.

title: Activities of Recombinant Human Cytochrome P450c27 (CYP27) Which Produce Intermediates of Alternative Bile Acid Biosynthetic Pathways
finding: Recombinant human CYP27A1 in a reconstituted system oxidised cholesterol to 27-hydroxycholesterol and then to the aldehyde and 3beta-hydroxy-5-cholestenoic acid, and further metabolised the acid to two monohydroxylated products at positions on the steroid nucleus. The substrates are the cholesterol series; the 7alpha-triol was not tested and 7alpha/7beta positions are excluded as hydroxylation sites for the acid.

title: Molecular Identification of d-Ribulokinase in Budding Yeast and Mammals
finding: Ribulose changed most in a yeast YDR109C deletion, and FGGY silencing in HEK293 cells raised ribulose (seen only with ribitol added); recombinant yeast and human FGGY preferred D-ribulose over other sugars. The authors speculate a metabolite-repair role.

title: A Single C-terminal Peptide Segment Mediates Both Membrane Association and Localization of Lysyl Hydroxylase in the Endoplasmic Reticulum
finding: A 40-residue C-terminal segment of lysyl hydroxylase 1, fused to a reporter, gave membrane association and ER retention in COS-7 cells (the first 25 residues matter most). The lumenal catalytic site is background in the paper, not tested; PLOD1 only.

title: Biochemical and genetic identity of alpha-keto acid reductase and cytoplasmic malate dehydrogenase from human erythrocytes
finding: Human erythrocyte aromatic alpha-keto acid reductase activity co-migrated with cytoplasmic malate dehydrogenase on starch gel, and antibody to MDH inhibited both; most reduction of aromatic keto acids in blood is due to MDH1, with a minor part by LDH. Erythrocyte and gel-electrophoresis evidence, not assays of the purified human enzymes.

title: Manipulation of [11C]-5-Hydroxytryptophan and 6-[18F]Fluoro-3,4-Dihydroxy-L-Phenylalanine Accumulation in Neuroendocrine Tumor Cells
finding: The human neuroendocrine tumor cell line BON took up labelled 5-hydroxytryptophan and the amino acid tracer FDOPA, and the amino-2-norbornanecarboxylic acid (system L inhibitor) blocked transport of both, so uptake is by a carrier; no gene is named. One cell line, tracer accumulation rather than secretion.

title: Pxmp2 Is a Channel-Forming Protein in Mammalian Peroxisomal Membrane
finding: Liver peroxisomes from Pxmp2 knockout mice kept part of their permeability to small solutes in vitro and in vivo, lost 1.3 nS channel activity, and recombinant and native Pxmp2 formed a weakly cation-selective pore of about 1.4 nm; the authors conclude cofactors and ATP need specific transporters. Mouse and insect-cell expression, not human.

title: A double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of n-3 fatty acid based lipid infusion in acute, extended guttate psoriasis
finding: In a 10-day trial of 20 psoriasis patients given n-3 or n-6 lipid infusions, ionophore-stimulated neutrophils generated leukotrienes; with the n-3 emulsion, LTA5 was measured as non-enzymatic degradation products (HPLC/UV). The non-enzymatic origin is assumed from the products, and the products were not identified by structure.

title: Molecular cloning and functional characterization of a GABA/betaine transporter from human kidney
finding: Cloned human BGT-1 (SLC6A12) from kidney and expressed it in 9HTEo- cells: GABA uptake had Km 20 uM and coupled to Na+ and Cl- with a stoichiometry of 3 Na+ : 2 Cl- : 1 GABA, derived from Hill coefficients. Betaine acts only as a competitive inhibitor of GABA uptake (about 500 uM), so betaine transport itself was not measured.

title: The permeability of human red blood cell membranes to hydrogen peroxide is independent of aquaporins
finding: H2O2 permeability of cholesterol-containing liposomes was 4e-4 (saturated) and 5e-3 cm/s (unsaturated acyl chains) at 37 C, and of human red cell membranes 1.6e-3 cm/s; AQP1 and AQP3 inhibitors had no effect and cells lacking AQP1 or AQP3 were as permeable as normal cells. Red cells and liposomes only; mitochondria were not studied, so the paper does not address AQP8 in mitochondrial H2O2 transport.

title: Physiological function and kinetic mechanism of human liver alcohol dehydrogenase as 5 beta-cholestane-3 alpha,7 alpha,12 alpha,26-tetrol dehydrogenase.
finding: The beta2beta2 isozyme of human liver alcohol dehydrogenase, purified from atypical livers, co-purified with 5beta-cholestane-3alpha,7alpha,12alpha,26-tetrol dehydrogenase activity; inhibitor sensitivity (phenanthroline, isobutyramide) was identical for both activities, so the authors conclude one active site catalyses both. Purified enzyme from atypical liver donors; the paper concerns the C26 tetrol oxidation.

title: New regulatory mechanisms in the biosynthesis of pheomelanins: rearrangement vs. redox exchange reaction routes of a transient 2H-1,4-benzothiazine-o-quinonimine intermediate
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - General Subjects
finding: Oxidation of 5-S-cysteinyldopa at physiological pH in vitro shows, by product yields and deuterium labelling, that the transient o-quinonimine undergoes redox exchange with cysteinyldopa to give the benzothiazine carboxylic acid DHBCA (QI + CD to DHBCA + cysteinyldopaquinone) or rearranges. Only the forward direction of this exchange is shown; no reversibility data, and the cysteinyldopaquinone + DOPA exchange (MAR06878) is mentioned only as background.

title: The Mechanisms of Human Hotdog-fold Thioesterase 2 (hTHEM2) Substrate Recognition and Catalysis Illuminated by a Structure and Function Based Analysis
finding: Substrate screen and crystal structure of human THEM2 (ACOT13, Q9NPJ3) with a substrate analogue: thioesterase activity occurs with acyl-CoAs (not acyl-ACP or acyl-Cys peptide), and medium-to-long-chain acyl-CoAs have the lowest Km. Recombinant enzyme in vitro; the authors propose a physiological role in cytosolic medium-to-long-chain acyl-CoA hydrolysis, and C14:1 and C17:1 acyl-CoAs were not tested.

title: Properties of the testicular lactate dehydrogenase isoenzyme
organism: Mus musculus;Columba livia;Homo sapiens;Bos taurus;Oryctolagus cuniculus
finding: LDH-X (LDHC) from mouse, pigeon and in sperm lysates of man, bull and rabbit converted 2-oxobutanoate and 2-oxopentanoate better than LDH 1 and LDH 5. Only the mouse enzyme used the branched 2-oxo acids well; pigeon, bull, rabbit and human LDH-X used them very poorly (Table 2), so branched-chain activity is not shown for human LDHC (see 10.1530/jrf.0.0550101).

title: No facilitator required for membrane transport of hydrogen sulfide
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
organism: in vitro (planar lipid bilayers; archaeal aquaporin AfAQP)
finding: In planar lipid bilayers, H2S permeability was at least 0.5 cm/s and did not change on reconstituting archaeal aquaporin AfAQP, which raised water permeability; the authors conclude that H2S crosses lipid membranes without a facilitator. Artificial bilayers only, H2S only (methanethiol not tested).

title: ATP1AL1, a Member of the Non-gastric H,K-ATPase Family, Functions as a Sodium Pump
finding: In HEK 293 cells expressing ATP1AL1 (ATP12A) with the gastric H,K-ATPase beta subunit, Na+ content was lower and a Na+ efflux inhibited only by 1 mM ouabain appeared; 86Rb+ influx matched this efflux, so the authors conclude the pair mediates mainly Na+,K+ exchange rather than H+,K+ exchange. One heterologous cell system with the gastric beta subunit; the in vivo partner is not shown.

title: Cytochrome P450 omega-Hydroxylase Pathway of Tocopherol Catabolism
finding: Tocopherols are catabolised by P450 omega-hydroxylation of the phytyl chain followed by stepwise chain shortening to the 3'-carboxychromanol; intermediates of gamma-tocopherol were identified by GC-MS in hepatocyte cultures, and among recombinant human P450s only CYP4F2 had omega-hydroxylase activity, with higher activity for gamma- than alpha-tocopherol. Rat and human liver microsomes and cultured hepatocytes.

title: Reassignment of the human aldehyde dehydrogenase ALDH8A1 (ALDH12) to the kynurenine pathway in tryptophan catabolism
finding: Bioinformatic and experimental evidence that human ALDH8A1 is the 2-aminomuconate semialdehyde dehydrogenase of the kynurenine pathway: the recombinant enzyme oxidised 2-AMS with NAD+ at an efficiency like the Pseudomonas fluorescens enzyme, and the product was identified by NMR and high-resolution MS. Recombinant enzyme in vitro.

title: Plasma and Urine Salsolinol in Humans: Effect of Acute Ethanol Intake on the Enantiomeric Composition of Salsolinol
finding: GC-MS enantiomer analysis in urine and plasma of 24 subjects found salsolinol racemic in healthy subjects, with no change in enantiomer ratio after 1 g/kg ethanol, contrary to earlier HPLC reports of predominant R in urine. This argues against an enantioselective enzymatic route in these subjects; total salsolinol output rose in only five subjects.

title: Uroporphyrinogen III Cosynthetase: A Direct Assay Method
organism: in vitro (cosynthetase assays; blood haemolysates, liver homogenates)
finding: Direct cosynthetase assay in which preuroporphyrinogen from porphobilinogen deaminase is converted much faster to uroporphyrinogen III by the cosynthetase than it decomposes non-enzymatically to uroporphyrinogen I; the non-enzymic product (about 0.1 nmol per assay) is subtracted as the blank. In vitro assay paper; Crossref lists 2017 for a reprint of the 1982 article.

title: Substrate specificity of the lactate dehydrogenase isoenzyme C4 from human spermatozoa and a possible selective assay
finding: Human sperm lysates (LDH C4 identified by zymogram) were active with pyruvate, 2-oxobutanoate, 2-oxopentanoate and 2-oxohexanoate but showed no activity with the branched 2-oxo acids 2-oxo-3-methylbutanoate, 2-oxo-3-methylpentanoate and 2-oxo-4-methylpentanoate that LDH C4 of other species uses. Supports LDHC on the straight-chain reaction (MAR05351) and contradicts it on the branched ones (MAR11476, MAR11479); see also 10.1042/bj1530165.

title: Fatty acid and cholesterol synthesis from specifically labeled leucine by isolated rat hepatocytes
finding: In isolated rat hepatocytes incubated with differently labelled leucine, with and without hydroxycitrate, radioactivity from the acetyl-CoA-labelled and the acetoacetate-labelled leucine entered fatty acids and cholesterol in patterns from which the authors conclude that mitochondrial HMG-CoA is not incorporated intact into cholesterol. Rat hepatocytes only; the conclusion is drawn from tracer labelling patterns, and no transporter is examined.

title: The sequence of a human mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase-encoding cDNA
finding: Reports the cDNA sequence from a HeLa library for human mitochondrial glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase (727 amino acids, 96% similar to the rat protein), with calmodulin-like Ca2+-binding sites and FAD- and putative glycerol-phosphate-binding sites. It is a sequence paper: the human enzyme, not E. coli GlpD, so it fits MAR00449 but is not evidence for the E. coli reference on MAR00483 (as cited in v2.0.1).

title: Sequential hydrolysis of FAD by ecto-5′ nucleotidase CD73 and alkaline phosphatase is required for uptake of vitamin B2 into cells
finding: In human cells, extracellular FAD is hydrolysed by CD73 to FMN and FMN by alkaline phosphatase to riboflavin, which is then imported; GPI-anchor-deficient cells lack both steps and have less intracellular vitamin B2. The cell work is on one human cell line (SH-SY5Y), and purified human bone ALP (ALPL) hydrolysed FMN in vitro; the intestinal isoform ALPI was not tested.

title: Characterization of the activity of purified recombinant human 5-lipoxygenase in the absence and presence of leukocyte factors.
finding: Purified recombinant human 5-lipoxygenase made 5-HPETE plus 6-trans-LTB4 and 12-epi-6-trans-LTB4, the non-enzymatic hydrolysis products of LTA4, identified by HPLC/UV against standards. In vitro with baculovirus-expressed enzyme only; the non-enzymatic products differ from the 12-epi-LTB4 (6Z) that the model reaction produces.

title: Determination of dopamine and dopamine-derived (R)-/(S)-salsolinol and norsalsolinol in various human brain areas using solid-phase extraction and gas chromatography/mass spectrometry
finding: Both salsolinol enantiomers were found by chiral GC/MS in 25 human post-mortem brains, with an (R)/(S) ratio of about 2, and levels did not correlate with dopamine. The authors interpret this as non-enzymatic Pictet-Spengler formation plus an additional enzymatic (R)-only synthesis; salsolinol-1-carboxylate (the pyruvate route) was not measured.

title: Retrieval-independent localization of lysyl hydroxylase in the endoplasmic reticulum via a peptide fold in its iron-binding domain
finding: Fusions of the last 40 residues of human lysyl hydroxylase 1 to a reporter (cathepsin D) were retained in the ER of COS-7 cells independently of the KDEL receptor and without Golgi-ER recycling; the minimal retention region is the last 32 residues, and 75 to 80 percent of the reporter was in the membrane fraction. Localization of the enzyme tail in one monkey cell line, not its reaction.

title: Aquaporin-3 mediates hydrogen peroxide uptake to regulate downstream intracellular signaling
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: With a fluorescent H2O2 probe, AQP3 and AQP8 increased H2O2 uptake into mammalian cells, but AQP1 did not, and endogenous AQP3 level changed intracellular H2O2 and growth-factor signalling. The AQP1 negative is from overexpression in the cells tested (the draft cites HEK293); the abstract does not name the cell line.

title: Human Placental Na+-dependent Multivitamin Transporter
finding: Cloned human SMVT from a placental choriocarcinoma cell line; expressed in HRPE cells and Xenopus oocytes it transports pantothenate, biotin and lipoate in a Na+-dependent way, with a Na+:vitamin stoichiometry of 2:1 from the sigmoidal Na+ dependence (Hill coefficient 1.9). Heterologous expression only; earlier 1:1 values came from native vesicles.

title: The Mammalian Cytosolic Selenoenzyme Thioredoxin Reductase Reduces Ubiquinone
finding: TrxR1 reduced ubiquinone-10 with NADPH or NADH at similar rates at pH 7.5 (apparent Km 22 µM), in a selenium-dependent way. The enzyme tested was purified bovine and recombinant rat TrxR1; human appears only as HEK293 homogenates with higher activity on overexpression.

title: Gat1 (Gaba:Na+:Cl−) Cotransport Function
finding: Giant membrane patches from Xenopus oocytes expressing GAT1 gave reversal potentials consistent with a stoichiometry of 1 GABA : 2 Na+ : 1 Cl-. Expression-system study; the species of the GAT1 clone is not stated in the abstract.

title: Identification of Human Cytochrome P450s Involved in the Formation of All-trans-Retinoic Acid Principal Metabolites
finding: Human liver microsomes and cDNA-expressed P450s formed 4-OH-RA and 4-oxo-RA mainly via CYP3A7, then CYP3A5, 2C8, 2C18, 3A4 and 2C9 (4-OH-RA by expressed P450s, ranked by Vmax/Km); CYP2B6 and 2A6 correlated with formation in liver microsomes. CYP26 enzymes and CYP2S1 are not among the P450s tested.

title: The bile acid synthetic gene 3β-hydroxy-Δ5-C27-steroid oxidoreductase is mutated in progressive intrahepatic cholestasis
finding: Expression cloning gave a microsomal liver C27 3beta-HSD (HSD3B7) that acted on four 7alpha-hydroxylated sterols when transfected into cultured cells but not on C19/C21 steroids; a 2-bp deletion in HSD3B7 in a patient with neonatal cholestasis abolished activity. Cell-transfection assays; mouse used for mRNA regulation, human for the gene and the patient mutation.

title: Supplementary data and scripts for \"An Atlas of Human Metabolism\"
finding: Zenodo dataset (Human1_Publication_Data_Scripts.zip) with the models, data and scripts of the Human1 paper (tINIT GEMs, ecGEMs and others); the draft cites the script compare_gene_essentiality_results.m for the statement that Human1 predicted genes absent from a context model as non-essential. The script was not opened here, so that statement is taken from the draft.

title: Hepatic microsomal metabolism of indole to indoxyl, a precursor of indoxyl sulfate
journal: European Journal of Drug Metabolism and Pharmacokinetics
finding: Rat liver microsomes with an NADPH-generating system oxidised indole to indoxyl (measured as indigo) with apparent Km 0.85 mM; inhibitor and inducer experiments showed P450 rather than FMO activity, and activity tracked CYP2E1 activity, so the authors conclude CYP2E1 is the major isoform. Rat microsomes only, no human enzyme tested.

title: A novel mammalian bubblegum-related acyl-CoA synthetase restricted to testes and possibly involved in spermatogenesis
finding: A newly characterised membrane-associated acyl-CoA synthetase (BGR, ACSBG2) showed activity on long- and very long-chain fatty acids; its human mRNA was detected only in testis, and mouse Bgr was found in testis germ and Sertoli cells. The abstract does not name stearate, so it does not show activity on that substrate.

authors: de los Ángeles Juricic M et al.
title: Salsolinol and isosalsolinol: Condensation products of acetaldehyde and dopamine. Separation of their enantiomers in the presence of a large excess of dopamine
journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Analysis
finding: An analytical methods paper: HPLC, NMR and MS showed commercial salsolinol contains about 10% isosalsolinol, and an HPLC method separates the (S)- and (R)-salsolinol enantiomers in the presence of excess dopamine. The condensation of dopamine with acetaldehyde in vitro, the pyruvate route and a putative (R)-salsolinol synthase are stated only as background (suggested or postulated), not shown.

title: Characterization of human sterol 27-hydroxylase. A mitochondrial cytochrome P-450 that catalyzes multiple oxidation reaction in bile acid biosynthesis.
finding: Human CYP27A1 cDNA expressed in COS cells catalysed repeated oxidation at C-27 of bile acid pathway sterols (CH3 to CH2OH to COOH), converting triol and tetrol substrates to the acid; the aldehyde intermediate was not detected, and mock-transfected cells oxidised slightly. Substrates are those of the cholic-acid branch; the 3a,7a-diol was not the substrate tested.

title: Transient quinonimines and 1,4-benzothiazines of pheomelanogenesis: new pulse radiolytic and spectrophotometric evidence
finding: Pulse radiolysis and ferricyanide oxidation gave spectral evidence for an o-quinonimine (absorbance maximum 540 nm) that forms by cyclisation of the o-quinone from 5-S-cysteinyldopa and then converts to unstable 1,4-benzothiazines. The cyclising species is the quinone (5-S-cysteinyldopaquinone), not 5-S-cysteinyldopa itself; chemistry in solution, no enzyme.

title: Identification and characterization of the vesicular GABA transporter
finding: Rat VGAT (homologue of C. elegans unc-47) expressed in transfected cells (PC12) mediated vesicular GABA transport with kinetics resembling brain synaptic vesicles, and its bioenergetic dependence differs from the monoamine transporter. Glycine uptake was not detected, which does not support a glycine reaction (MAR07737); no beta-alanine data (MAR07736). Rat and worm, not human.

title: Proline dehydrogenase 2 (PRODH2) is a hydroxyproline dehydrogenase (HYPDH) and molecular target for treating primary hyperoxaluria
finding: Purified recombinant human PRODH2 (catalytic core residues 157-515, one FAD) prefers hydroxyproline over proline, with a 12-fold higher kcat/Km, and the authors propose it uses CoQ10 as the electron acceptor in vivo and rename it HYPDH. The paper does not discuss hyperprolinaemia.

title: Identification of the human cytochrome P450, P450RAI-2, which is predominantly expressed in the adult cerebellum and is responsible for all-trans-retinoic acid metabolism
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Transiently transfected P450RAI-2 (CYP26B1) converted all-trans-retinoic acid to 4-oxo-, 4-OH- and 18-OH-all-trans-retinoic acid, with retinoic acid the preferred substrate in competition experiments; mRNA was highest in adult cerebellum and pons. The abstract does not name the host cells.

title: 4-Hydroxyretinoic Acid, a Novel Substrate for Human Liver Microsomal UDP-glucuronosyltransferase(s) and Recombinant UGT2B7
finding: Human liver microsomes and recombinant UGT2B7 glucuronidated all-trans-retinoic acid, 4-hydroxy-retinoic acid and 4-hydroxy-retinyl acetate, with microsomal activity on 4-hydroxy-retinoic acid 6-fold that on retinoic acid; retinoic acid, 4-oxo- and 5,6-epoxy-retinoic acid gave carboxyl-linked glucuronides. The authors postulate a key role for UGT2B7.

title: PTEN M-CBR3, a Versatile and Selective Regulator of Inositol 1,3,4,5,6-Pentakisphosphate (Ins(1,3,4,5,6)P5)
finding: In U87-MG cells wild-type PTEN did not regulate inositol phosphate levels, whereas the engineered mutant PTEN M-CBR3 lowered Ins(1,3,4,5,6)P5 by 60%. One glioblastoma cell line; contradicts the activity of wild-type PTEN on this substrate reported in 10.1016/s0014-5793(01)02500-5 (Caffrey 2001).

title: Cloning of Dimethylglycine Dehydrogenase and a New Human Inborn Error of Metabolism, Dimethylglycine Dehydrogenase Deficiency
journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
finding: DMGDH is described as a mitochondrial matrix enzyme converting dimethylglycine to sarcosine with FAD and folate; one adult patient with raised dimethylglycine carried a homozygous H109R change that inactivated the enzyme on expression. One patient; the mitochondrial location is stated as background.

title: An evolutionarily conserved gene family encodes proton-selective ion channels
finding: Otopetrin1 forms a proton-selective channel required for zinc-sensitive proton conductance in mouse acid-sensing taste cells, and mouse Otop2 and Otop3 and a Drosophila ortholog also encode proton channels. The abstract tests mouse and fly proteins, not the human OTOPs.

title: Identification of a new inborn error in bile acid synthesis: mutation of the oxysterol 7alpha-hydroxylase gene causes severe neonatal liver disease.
finding: One infant with severe cholestasis and a nonsense mutation in CYP7B1 (no enzyme activity in liver microsomes or on expression) had 3beta-hydroxy-5-cholenoic and 3beta-hydroxy-5-cholestenoic acids as 96% of serum bile acids and 27-hydroxycholesterol over 4,500 times normal, showing that 7alpha-hydroxylation in the acidic pathway needs CYP7B1. A single patient.

title: Enzymatic, metabolic and secretory patterns in human islets of Type 2 (non-insulin-dependent) diabetic patients
finding: Islets isolated from cadaveric donors had lower FAD-linked glycerophosphate dehydrogenase activity, and lower glucose utilisation, glucose oxidation and glucose-induced insulin release, in Type 2 diabetic patients than in non-diabetic controls; the authors link the enzyme deficit to the glycerol phosphate shuttle. A human tissue-level activity measurement, not a gene-level or structural study of the enzyme.

title: Transport and transporters in the endoplasmic reticulum
finding: Review of transport across the ER membrane: the authors conclude that the transport processes studied so far are protein-mediated and often rate-limiting for luminal enzymes, and that few transporter proteins are identified. It does not mention 2-oxoglutarate or succinate carriers, so it does not support a statement that no ER carrier exists for them; it reports passage of some low-mass anions (e.g. UDP-glucuronate) through the translocon channel in rat microsomes, a weak result. A cited review of MAR06512 (FAD transport) is not checked here beyond the abstract.

title: Mitochondrial aquaporin-8 knockdown in human hepatoma HepG2 cells causes ROS-induced mitochondrial depolarization and loss of viability
finding: siRNA knockdown of mitochondrial AQP8 (about 60 percent protein loss) in HepG2 cells reduced H2O2 release from isolated mitochondria by about 45 percent, raised mitochondrial ROS and depolarised the mitochondria through the permeability transition pore, with loss of viability; the authors conclude that mtAQP8 facilitates mitochondrial H2O2 release. One hepatoma cell line; contradicted for liver mitochondria by Yang 2006 (10.1074/jbc.M601864200), which finds the same water permeability without AQP8.

title: Urinary excretion of 2,7,8-trimethyl-2-(beta-carboxyethyl)-6-hydroxychroman is a major route of elimination of gamma-tocopherol in humans
finding: GC-MS of 24 h urine pools from healthy subjects after glucuronidase treatment gave 4.6 to 29.8 micromol gamma-CEHC per day (2.5 to 31.5 micromol/g creatinine); the authors conclude that conversion of gamma-tocopherol to gamma-CEHC, then glucuronidation and urinary excretion, is a major elimination route in humans. Measures the excreted product, not the enzymes.

title: The non-oxidative degradation of ascorbic acid at physiological conditions
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: At pH 7.0 and 37 degrees C, L-erythrulose and oxalate were the main degradation products of ascorbate, dehydroascorbate and 2,3-diketogulonate, identified by 13C NMR and HPLC; the molar yield of erythrulose from 2,3-diketogulonate was high (about 97 percent given in the abstract). Chemistry in buffer, no enzyme involved, so it supports a spontaneous reaction only in vitro.

title: A voltage-gated proton-selective channel lacking the pore domain
finding: The mammalian voltage-sensor-domain protein HV1 (HVCN1) alone produces a voltage-gated, pH-gradient-sensitive, H+-selective, Zn2+-inhibited current, and the authors identify it as the long-sought voltage-gated proton channel needed for the leukocyte oxidative burst. Established by heterologous expression and mutagenesis; the abstract does not state the species of the expressed clone.

title: The role of cytoplasmic free calcium in the responses of quin2-loaded human platelets to vasopressin
finding: Quin2-loaded human platelets had a basal cytosolic free Ca2+ of about 100 nM (127 +/- 10 nM) and vasopressin raised it to about 700 nM in 1 mM external Ca2+, mainly by influx across the plasma membrane. The 1 mM figure is the medium concentration, not a measured in vivo gradient; the direction of net influx is inferred.

title: Expression cloning of a reserpine-sensitive vesicular monoamine transporter
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Rat vesicular monoamine transporter 1 (cDNA expression-cloned in CV-1 cells) took up serotonin ATP-dependently (Km 1.3 micromolar) in digitonin-permeabilised cells, was abolished by an uncoupler and by a V-ATPase inhibitor, and ranked serotonin above dopamine and norepinephrine as substrate. Rat protein, no stoichiometry measured, catecholamine transport inferred from inhibition potency only; not human.

title: Lysyl Hydroxylase 3 Is a Multifunctional Protein Possessing Collagen Glucosyltransferase Activity
finding: Human lysyl hydroxylase isoform 3 has both lysyl hydroxylase and collagen glucosyltransferase activity, while LH1 and LH2 lack the glucosyltransferase activity; antibodies partly inhibited the activity in fibroblast extracts and mutagenesis separated the two active sites. Galactosyltransferase activity was not tested, so it supports the glucosylation step (MAR06985) but not the galactosylation (MAR06984).

title: Mammalian Wax Biosynthesis
finding: Two mouse fatty acyl-CoA reductases, FAR1 and FAR2, were shown by expression in cells to reduce fatty acids to fatty alcohols, FAR1 acting on fatty acyl-CoA esters with NADPH as cofactor and preferring 16 or 18 carbon chains; both localised to peroxisomes by confocal microscopy and were expressed in wax- and ether-lipid-rich tissues. Mouse enzymes in cell expression, no kinetic constants in the abstract; shows the reaction is a fatty acyl-CoA reductase, not a formate dehydrogenase.

title: The Endoplasmic Reticulum Membrane Is Permeable to Small Molecules
finding: Isolated ER vesicles (dog) and permeabilised cells let small chemical modification reagents, including a small charged one, cross passively into the lumen, while a roughly 5 kDa reagent did not, so the ER membrane is leaky to small molecules compared with the plasma, lysosomal and trans-Golgi membranes. Non-physiological probes only; 2-oxoglutarate and succinate were not tested, so this is weak support for their passage.

title: Structure of V-ATPase from the mammalian brain
finding: Cryo-EM structure of rat brain V-ATPase, with a ten-protomer c ring, defines an ATP:proton ratio of 3:10. Rat enzyme, structural inference of the ratio; for the T2 name row on VMAT it is background only.

title: The human collagen beta(1-O)galactosyltransferase, GLT25D1, is a soluble endoplasmic reticulum localized protein
finding: Epitope-tagged human GLT25D1 (COLGALT1) expressed in Huh7 cells localised to the ER lumen as a soluble, ER-retained glycoprotein and overlapped with LH3 (PLOD3) and mannose-binding lectin. Overexpressed tagged protein in one hepatoma cell line.

title: Purine nucleoside phosphorylases purified from rat liver and novikoff hepatoma cells
finding: Purine nucleoside phosphorylase was purified from rat liver and from Novikoff hepatoma cells and its properties compared between the two sources. Nicotinate riboside was not among the substrates tested, so the paper gives no support for phosphorolysis of nicotinate riboside; rat enzyme only, in vitro.
locator: Full text (substrate specificity; no nicotinate riboside tested)

title: A preliminary account of the properties of recombinant human Glyoxylate reductase (GRHPR), LDHA and LDHB with glyoxylate, and their potential roles in its metabolism
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Proteins and Proteomics
finding: Purified recombinant human LDHA, LDHB and GRHPR were assayed with glyoxylate and hydroxypyruvate: Km for glyoxylate reduction was 29.3 mM (LDHA), 9.9 mM (LDHB) and 1.0 mM (GRHPR), and glyoxylate oxidation by LDHA and LDHB had Km of 0.18 and 0.26 mM. Only LDHA and LDHB were tested among the lactate dehydrogenases, so nothing is shown for LDHC or LDHAL6A; in vitro with recombinant protein.

title: Restricted role for methionine synthase reductase defined by subcellular localization
finding: A GFP fusion of the N-terminal extension of the long MTRR (MSR) isoform did not reach mitochondria in human fibroblasts, and antibodies placed endogenous MSR in the cytosol and not in mitochondria in fibroblasts and Huh-1 hepatoma cells (Western blot, immunofluorescence). The authors conclude MSR is cytosolic and suggest a similar, mitochondrial protein may act with MMAB; note it rests on the Leal in vitro result (10.1074/jbc.M405449200) that MSR with MMAB can reduce cob(II)alamin.

title: Phytanic acid and pristanic acid are oxidized by sequential peroxisomal and mitochondrial reactions in cultured fibroblasts
finding: Acylcarnitine profiling by tandem MS in control and mutant human fibroblasts showed that phytanic and pristanic acid are first oxidised in peroxisomes to 4,8-dimethylnonanoyl-CoA, exported as its carnitine ester (presumably via peroxisomal carnitine octanoyltransferase), and further oxidised in mitochondria after transfer by carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase and CPT2 (CPT1 not needed), giving 2,6-dimethylheptanoyl-CoA. The abstract names no enzyme for the mitochondrial oxidation of 4,8-dimethylnonanoyl-CoA itself.

title: Stable Isotopomers of myo-Inositol Uncover a Complex MINPP1-Dependent Inositol Phosphate Network
finding: 13C-labelled myo-inositol and inositol phosphates followed by NMR and CE-MS in human cells revealed a branch of inositol phosphate dephosphorylation that depends on MINPP1, whose activity was also characterised in vitro and in cells. The abstract does not state the position-specific Ins(1,3,4,5,6)P5 3-phosphatase step or any PTEN activity; verify the step in the full text before relying on it.

title: Recon3D enables a three-dimensional view of gene variation in human metabolism
finding: Presents the Recon3D human metabolic reconstruction (3,288 open reading frames, 13,543 reactions, 4,140 unique metabolites, 12,890 protein structures) as a computational model; it is a source model, not an experiment, so a reaction taken from it carries no measurement unless the reaction has its own reference.

title: Dual metabolic pathway of 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 catalyzed by human CYP24
finding: Human CYP24 expressed in E. coli with adrenodoxin and adrenodoxin reductase converted 25(OH)D3 and 1alpha,25(OH)2D3 along both a C-23 hydroxylation route (to the 26,23-lactone) and a C-24 route (via 24-oxo intermediates to tetranor-23(OH)D3), unlike rat CYP24 which lacked the C-23 route. Recombinant bacterial system only; vitamin D2 substrates not covered.

title: Distinct pharmacological properties and distribution in neurons and endocrine cells of two isoforms of the human vesicular monoamine transporter
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Human VMAT1 and VMAT2 expressed in digitonin-permeabilised CV-1 cells differ in affinity and tissue distribution; only serotonin uptake was measured directly (catecholamines and histamine as inhibition constants), H+ dependence is noted, and proton stoichiometry per amine was not measured.
locator: Full text (p.5167 and transport experiments); Abstract

title: Vesicular Inhibitory Amino Acid Transporter Is a Cl-/gamma-Aminobutyrate Co-transporter
finding: Purified VIAAT in proteoliposomes took up GABA (and glycine) driven by membrane potential but not by pH gradient, required Cl- and co-transported it (about one GABA to two Cl- equivalents per cycle); mutation E213A abolished transport. In vitro; the abstract does not give the species of the protein and shows no H+ coupling, so it does not support a proton-antiport stoichiometry.

title: omega-Oxidation of 20-Hydroxyeicosatetraenoic Acid (20-HETE) in Cerebral Microvascular Smooth Muscle and Endothelium by Alcohol Dehydrogenase 4
finding: Mouse brain microvascular smooth muscle and endothelial cells converted 20-HETE to 20-COOH-AA, which an ADH inhibitor reduced; purified mouse and human ADH4 (also ADH3 and horse ADH1) oxidised 20-HETE in vitro, and ADH4 is judged mainly responsible in these cells. Human enzyme shown only as purified protein.

title: The human Cas1 protein: A sialic acid-specific O-acetyltransferase?
finding: Human CASD1 (Cas1) tagged with GFP localised to medial and trans Golgi; co-overexpression with GD3 synthase raised 7-O-acetylated GD3 by up to 40 percent, CASD1 mRNA was up to 5-fold higher in tumour cells with O-Ac-GD3, and CASD1 siRNA lowered O-acetylation. The authors suggest direct involvement in O-acetylation of alpha2-8-linked sialic acids; the product is 7-O-acetyl GD3, in cultured cells.

title: Inhibition of aquaporin-1 prevents myocardial remodeling by blocking the transmembrane transport of hydrogen peroxide
finding: Cardiac myocytes: AQP1 sits at the plasma membrane with NADPH oxidase-2, and its deletion or pore blockade inhibited H2O2 transport in mouse and human cells and rescued hypertrophy in iPSC-derived human engineered heart muscle; the authors conclude AQP1 mediates H2O2 entry in cardiomyocytes. Cardiomyocytes only; other cell types are not covered.

title: iAB-RBC-283: A proteomically derived knowledge-base of erythrocyte metabolism that can be used to simulate its physiological and patho-physiological states
finding: Proteomics-based reconstruction of mature erythrocyte metabolism with 281 enzymes, curated from literature and functionally tested; it is a model, not a measurement of any single transport step. The abstract says nothing about a proton channel or proton transport.

title: Decreased availability of GDP-l-fucose in a patient with LAD II with normal GDP-d-mannose dehydratase and FX protein activities
finding: A newly identified leukocyte adhesion deficiency type II patient had severe hypofucosylation, yet cytosolic extracts of the patient's leukocytes and fibroblasts made GDP-L-fucose from GDP-D-mannose normally in vitro, and the GDP-mannose 4,6-dehydratase and FX protein (TSTA3) transcripts were normal in amount with no coding mutations. The authors conclude that the main GDP-L-fucose synthesis pathway can be intact in this disorder, contrary to an earlier report (Sturla 1998); the paper does not measure FX protein enzymology beyond the extract assay.

title: Two chinese hamster ovary glycosylation mutants affected in the conversion of GDP-mannose to GDP-fucose
finding: Cytosol of the CHO lectin-resistant mutant Lec13 made no detectable GDP-fucose or GDP-sugar intermediates from GDP-mannose, and mixing experiments placed the block at GDP-mannose 4,6-dehydratase (EC 4.2.1.47); Lec13A cytosol made reduced amounts and its dehydratase activity was less pH sensitive, so the authors suggest an altered enzyme. The paper concerns the dehydratase step and does not assay the 3,5-epimerase/4-reductase step that MAR08768 represents; hamster cell mutants only (gene assignment GMDS is not stated in the abstract).

title: Transport of histamine by vesicular monoamine transporter-2
finding: In a heterologous expression system VMAT2 took up 3H-histamine, which was also an inhibitor of serotonin transport by VMAT2 but not VMAT1; histamine did not displace 3H-reserpine, and reserpine blocked histamine transport much less potently than serotonin transport. Mutating serines in transmembrane domain 3 abolished histamine transport. Only VMAT2 was tested as a histamine carrier in this abstract; the species of the transporter is not given in the abstract and the VMAT1 result is inhibition-based, not a transport assay.

title: Comparison of the function and expression of CYP26A1 and CYP26B1, the two retinoic acid hydroxylases
finding: Recombinant CYP26A1 and CYP26B1 formed the same primary and sequential metabolites from all-trans-retinoic acid, with 4-OH-RA, 18-OH-RA and 4-oxo-RA all accepted as substrates; for 4-OH-RA formation CYP26B1 had Km 19 nM and Vmax 0.8 pmol/min/pmol and CYP26A1 Km 50 nM and Vmax 10 pmol/min/pmol, with CYP26A1 2 to 10 times more active on all substrates. mRNA and protein of both isoforms correlated across human tissues, with CYP26B1 dominant in cerebellum and CYP26A1 in liver. Only CYP26A1 and CYP26B1 are examined, so the other P450s in the model rules are not supported by this paper.

title: Tumor-Repopulating Cells Induce PD-1 Expression in CD8+ T Cells by Transferring Kynurenine and AhR Activation
finding: Tumor-repopulating cells released kynurenine in response to interferon-gamma from CD8+ T cells, and the kynurenine entered adjacent CD8+ T cells through SLC7A8 and PAT4 (SLC36A4), activating AhR and raising PD-1 expression; the pathway was confirmed in tumor-bearing mice and cancer patients. SLC7A8 and PAT4 are named as the T-cell kynurenine uptake transporters, mainly shown in mouse systems; the paper does not name SLC7A5 or SLC3A2.

title: A Shared Vesicular Carrier Allows Synaptic Corelease of GABA and Glycine
finding: Mouse Viaat (VGAT) knockout caused embryonic lethality, omphalocele and cleft palate and sharply reduced transmitter release from both GABAergic and glycinergic neurons, indicating that glycinergic neurons have no separate vesicular glycine transporter; GABA and glycine compete for vesicular uptake. Knockout phenotype in mouse neurons; vesicular transport stoichiometry is not measured.

title: The chromaffin granule and synaptic vesicle amine transporters differ in substrate recognition and sensitivity to inhibitors.
finding: A side-by-side comparison showed the brain-type vesicular amine transporter (SVAT, VMAT2) has higher affinity than the adrenal chromaffin granule type (CGAT, VMAT1) for monoamine substrates, especially histamine, about 10-fold higher tetrabenazine sensitivity, and binds dihydrotetrabenazine while CGAT does not. Methamphetamine inhibited SVAT more than CGAT by competing at the amine site rather than by dissipating the pH gradient. Transport assays of the two cloned transporters; species of each clone is not given in the abstract.

title: Proton: substrate stoichiometries during active transport of biogenic amines in chromaffin ghosts.
finding: In isolated chromaffin ghosts, ATP generated a proton gradient (acidic inside) and a positive-inside membrane potential that drove biogenic amine accumulation; the driving force fitted membrane potential minus 2 times Z times the pH difference, so each amine was taken up in exchange for protons, which the authors present as evidence for an obligatory coupled exchange via a reserpine-sensitive carrier. The abstract does not state the number of protons per amine as a count, and the species (bovine chromaffin ghosts) is taken from the tissue type, not stated in the abstract.

title: Kinetic Parameters for the Vesicular Acetylcholine Transporter: Two Protons Are Exchanged for One Acetylcholine
finding: Transport and ligand-binding kinetics of synaptic vesicles from the Torpedo electric organ, analysed at varied internal and external pH, ACh concentration and membrane potential, fitted a two-proton model for the vesicular acetylcholine transporter much better than a one-proton model, and uptake rose at more positive internal potential as that model predicts. The authors derive pKa values and rate constants for the transport cycle; the study is on Torpedo vesicles, not human VAChT.

title: Tumor cell-released kynurenine biases MEP differentiation into megakaryocytes in individuals with cancer by activating AhR–RUNX1
finding: Tumor cells released large amounts of kynurenine that megakaryocytic-erythroid progenitor cells took up through SLC7A8, activating AhR and RUNX1 to bias differentiation toward megakaryocytes, with activated AhR raising SLC7A8 expression in a positive feedback; this was shown in humanized mice and in individuals with cancer. SLC7A8 is the named kynurenine uptake route in MEPs; the abstract does not name SLC7A5 or SLC3A2.

title: L-tryptophan reacts with naturally occurring and food-occurring phenolic aldehydes to give phenolic tetrahydro-beta-carboline alkaloids: activity as antioxidants and free radical scavengers
journal: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
finding: Benzaldehyde and several phenolic aldehydes condensed with L-tryptophan in aqueous acid (heat needed for all but benzaldehyde) to give tetrahydro-beta-carboline-3-carboxylic acids as cis and trans isomers. The study shows aldehyde condensation only: the product is the tetrahydro acid, not the aromatic beta-carboline, and tryptophan without an aldehyde was not tested.

title: The third activity for lysyl hydroxylase 3: galactosylation of hydroxylysyl residues in collagens in vitro
finding: Recombinant human lysyl hydroxylase 3 transfers galactose to hydroxylysyl residues in collagen in vitro, in addition to its hydroxylase and glucosyltransferase activities.

title: Core Glycosylation of Collagen Is Initiated by Two β(1-O)Galactosyltransferases
finding: GLT25D1 and GLT25D2 are the β(1-O)galactosyltransferases of collagen glycosylation; no galactosyltransferase activity was detected for lysyl hydroxylase 3.

title: Molecular characterization of the human peroxisomal branchedchain acyl-CoA oxidase: cDNA cloning, chromosomal assignment, tissue distribution, and evidence for the absence of the protein in Zellweger syndrome
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
finding: Cloned and sequenced the human liver branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase, the enzyme purified earlier as the oxidase of 2-methyl-branched acyl-CoAs and of the bile acid intermediates, and showed from sequence identity (74 percent), antibody cross-reactivity and a phylogenetic tree that it is the human homolog of rat trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA oxidase and not of rat pristanoyl-CoA oxidase. The mRNA is present in liver, kidney, heart and other tissues, and the protein is not detectable in Zellweger liver. Limits: enzyme activity of the recombinant protein was not measured here; the authors state that rat pristanoyl-CoA oxidase is apparently not expressed in human, a view that Ferdinandusse 2018 revised for ACOX3
locator: Results and Discussion, The BRCACox Is the Human Counterpart of rTHCCox; Fig. 3; Conclusions

title: The CoA esters of 2-methyl-branched chain fatty acids and of the bile acid intermediates di- and trihydroxycoprostanic acids are oxidized by one single peroxisomal branched chain acyl-CoA oxidase in human liver and kidney
finding: From human liver and kidney, a 70 kDa oxidase was partly purified in which the activities with 2-methylpalmitoyl-CoA, pristanoyl-CoA and trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA stayed together through phenyl, cation-exchange, gel filtration and hydroxylapatite columns, while palmitoyl-CoA oxidase separated as a different enzyme. The authors found no separate trihydroxycoprostanoyl-CoA oxidase in human liver. The enzyme also acted weakly on straight-chain acyl-CoAs. Limits: partly purified preparations, activity followed as hydrogen peroxide; the stereoisomer of the bile acid intermediate is not stated in the text; the gene was identified later (Baumgart 1996)
locator: Results, Purification (Figs 3 to 8) and Substrate Specificity (Table III); Discussion

title: Carnitine palmitoyltransferase 2: New insights on the substrate specificity and implications for acylcarnitine profiling
journal: Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Molecular Basis of Disease
finding: Recombinant human CPT2 in yeast homogenate, assayed from acyl-CoA and carnitine to acylcarnitine, was active on saturated acyl-CoAs from C8 to C20 (highest at C10 to C14, C20:0 about a fifth of C16:0 in the bars of Fig. 1A), on cis-9 C18:1 and the C14:1 acyl-CoAs, and showed virtually no activity with short-chain acyl-CoAs (C2 to C6), with C24:0, C26:0 and cis-15 C24:1 in Fig. 1, with trans-2-enoyl-CoAs (1 to 1.5 percent of the saturated rate) or with branched-chain amino acid intermediates. Polyunsaturated and odd-chain acyl-CoAs and C21 to C23 were not tested. Limits: in vitro, yeast homogenate; the text gives the active range as C14 to C18 in the abstract and C8 to C20 in the Discussion; per-chain values were read from the bars of Fig. 1
locator: Results 3.1 and Fig. 1A to D; Table 1; Discussion

title: Metabolic Interplay between Peroxisomes and Other Subcellular Organelles Including Mitochondria and the Endoplasmic Reticulum
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
finding: Review that names ACOX2 (branched-chain acyl-CoA oxidase) as the prime oxidase of pristanoyl-CoA and of the CoA esters of the bile acid intermediates DHCA and THCA (citing Vanhove 1993), lists ACOX2, D-bifunctional protein and SCPx as the enzymes of THCA-CoA beta-oxidation, states that peroxisomes hold the carnitine acyltransferases CrAT and CrOT acting on short and medium-chain acyl-CoAs, that carnitine is needed to carry the end products of peroxisomal beta-oxidation to mitochondria and not to take fatty acids up, and that peroxisomes chain-shorten fatty acids to acetyl-CoA, propionyl-CoA and medium-chain acyl-CoAs. It names two peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidases and does not mention ACOX3. Limits: a review; the claims carry the citations of the underlying studies
locator: Fatty Acid Beta-Oxidation; Bile Acid Synthesis; Peroxisomal Beta-Oxidation and the Interplay with Mitochondria

title: Cloning, Expression, and Fatty Acid Regulation of the Human Δ-5 Desaturase
finding: Cloned the human gene that lies about 11 kb from the delta-6 desaturase gene (accession AF126799, FADS2) and showed by stable expression in CHO cells that it converts 20:3 n-6 to 20:4 n-6 (over 12 percent in 24 hours) and does not convert 18:3 n-3 to 18:4 n-3, so it is the delta-5 desaturase (FADS1). Limits: the lack of delta-6 activity is reported as data not shown; one cell line; FADS2 on delta-5 substrates was not tested
locator: Results and Discussion, Expression of D-5 Desaturase in CHO Cells; Fig. 2

title: cDNA cloning and characterization of human Δ5-desaturase involved in the biosynthesis of arachidonic acid
finding: Cloned the human delta-5 desaturase cDNA (AF226273, FADS1) and showed in mouse L cells that it converts dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid to arachidonic acid and C20:4 n-3 to eicosapentaenoic acid. In serum-free medium without added gamma-linolenic acid, gamma-linolenic acid stayed undetectable in the transfected cells as in the control cells, which shows no delta-6 activity on linoleate in that condition. Limits: mouse cell expression; the delta-6 result is an undetectable product, not a dedicated assay; FADS2 was not expressed
locator: Results, Expression of delta-5-desaturase in L cells; Tables 1 and 2; Discussion

title: The liver isoform of carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1 is not targeted to the endoplasmic reticulum
finding: In rat liver, the malonyl-CoA-sensitive carnitine acyltransferase of microsomal fractions behaves as the 88 kDa liver CPT1 derived from mitochondria, probably from contact sites, and not as an ER-targeted enzyme: full-length CPT1-EGFP stayed in mitochondria in COS-1 cells, in vitro translated CPT1 did not insert authentically into canine pancreatic microsomes, and porin showed that microsomal fractions hold mitochondria-derived membranes. The authors state that this does not exclude a malonyl-CoA-insensitive luminal carnitine acyltransferase. Limits: rat; the contact-site origin is a proposal; a result in HeLa cells is cited from another study

title: Membrane transport of fatty acylcarnitine and free l‐carnitine by rat liver microsomes
finding: Sealed rat liver microsomes (97.5 percent latency of a luminal acyl-CoA:ethanol acyltransferase, impermeable to palmitoyl-CoA) took up palmitoylcarnitine, which a luminal carnitine acyltransferase turned into palmitoyl-CoA using a luminal CoASH pool (indirect reporter assay, about 939 pmol per min per mg at 30 C), and took up free carnitine without saturation up to 10 mM, inhibited by mersalyl but not by N-ethylmaleimide or sulfobetaine, unlike the mitochondrial carnitine/acylcarnitine carrier. The carrier or channel and the luminal enzyme were not identified. Limits: rat; indirect reporter; crude minimum rates; only palmitoyl substrates; several controls shown as data not shown

title: The medium-chain carnitine acyltransferase activity associated with rat liver microsomes is malonyl-CoA sensitive
finding: Rat liver microsomes contain a membrane-bound carnitine acyltransferase that uses decanoyl-CoA (Vmax about ten times that of palmitoyl-CoA) and palmitoyl-CoA, is inhibited by malonyl-CoA (50 percent at 5.3 uM, 87 percent on average at 17 uM over 25 preparations) while carnitine acetyltransferase is not, and is inhibited by palmitoyl-CoA at higher concentration. Antibody against mitochondrial CPT did not inhibit it and antibody against peroxisomal COT inhibited only 17 percent. Marker enzymes put mitochondrial contamination below 3 percent and peroxisomal marker at 9.6 percent. Limits: not purified; kinetic constants not determined; Broadway 2003 later attributes the malonyl-CoA-sensitive activity to mitochondria-derived CPT1
locator: Abstract; Results (Tables I and II; Figs 1 to 5); Discussion

title: Properties of the medium chain/long chain carnitine acyltransferase purified from rat liver microsomes.
finding: A 53 kDa monomeric carnitine acyltransferase purified from rat liver microsomes acts on saturated acyl-CoAs from C6 to C16 with similar K0.5 (1 to 4 uM), not on butyryl-CoA, and chains above C16 were not tested. After purification it is not inhibited by malonyl-CoA and only weakly by etomoxiryl-CoA. Antibodies against mitochondrial CPT or peroxisomal CAT do not react with it, and an N-terminal sequence added in proof is not a known carnitine acyltransferase but resembles ER proteins. The reaction is reversible. Limits: the purified enzyme was only partly active in the reverse direction; sidedness was not examined; no gene identified
locator: Abstract; Results, Table I and Table II; Discussion; Note Added in Proof

title: The Subcellular Distribution of Carnitine Acyltransferases in Mammalian Liver and Kidney
finding: In density gradients of rat and pig liver and kidney, about half of the liver carnitine acetyltransferase activity was mitochondrial, 14 percent peroxisomal and about a third in a light, lipid-rich membrane fraction that included microsomes; microsome fractions isolated by differential centrifugation also had activity (contamination below 3 percent by catalase and cytochrome c oxidase). Carnitine palmitoyltransferase was found only in mitochondria and was very low or not detectable in microsomes. Limits: only acetyl-, octanoyl- and palmitoyl-CoA were used; the light fraction holds more than one organelle; the scan is partly garbled in the extracted text

title: Microsomal malonyl-CoA-sensitive carnitine acyltransferase
finding: Short review that describes two carnitine acyltransferase activities in rat liver microsomes, a malonyl-CoA-sensitive one on the cytosolic face and a malonyl-CoA-insensitive one in the lumen, summarises antibody and etomoxir labelling that point to an 88 kDa polypeptide like CPT1 in microsomes, and states that cDNA experiments gave no support for ER targeting of CPT1. The identity of the luminal enzyme is left open. Limits: mostly restates cited work; some experiments are unpublished
locator: Abstract; main text on the two activities and on CPT1 targeting

title: Carnitine Acyltransferases and Associated Transport Processes in the Endoplasmic Reticulum
journal: Advances in Experimental Medicine and Biology
finding: Book chapter that describes the two microsomal carnitine acyltransferases of rat liver and a transport route for acylcarnitine and free carnitine across the ER membrane, proposes that luminal fatty acyl-CoA is supplied through acylcarnitine for triacylglycerol assembly in VLDL, and states that the identity of the luminal enzyme is still open and that a protein disulfide isomerase family candidate showed no carnitine acyltransferase activity when expressed. The authors call the physiological role open. Limits: a review; the claims carry the citations of the underlying studies
locator: Sections on the two microsomal CATs, on transport, and on VLDL assembly
